items.title: Deep learning retinal vein occlusion diagnosis: a systematic review and meta-analysis
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: The diagnosis of retinal vein occlusion (RVO) requires specialised imaging and clinician expertise. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to quantitatively synthesise the current state of artificial intelligence models dedicated to RVO diagnosis. METHODS: Cochrane Central, Embase, Ovid Medline, and PubMed were searched from inception to June 28, 2025. We included studies that evaluated deep learning models for RVO diagnosis and were validated on clinical datasets. The primary outcomes were the accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity of deep learning models for RVO diagnosis. Risk of bias was assessed using the Quality Assessment of Diagnostic Accuracy Studies 2 tool. RESULTS: Of 612 studies screened, 27 met the inclusion criteria, and 15 were included in the meta-analysis. Pooled deep learning model performance for RVO diagnosis was as follows: 97.4% accuracy (95% confidence interval [CI] 95.0%-98.7%), 89.9% sensitivity (95% CI 85.3%-93.3%), and 98.6% specificity (95% CI 96.5%-99.4%). Models predominantly used colour fundus photography (n = 18), OCT (n = 6), and ultra-widefield imaging (n = 2). Despite substantial heterogeneity, overall study quality was acceptable. In the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation assessment, reasons for downgrading were inconsistency and imprecision. CONCLUSIONS: Deep learning models showed high diagnostic accuracy in detecting retinal vein occlusion across different imaging modalities. However, the certainty of the evidence, assessed using Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation, was low for all outcomes. Future research should investigate the feasibility and costs of implementing deep learning for RVO diagnosis in real-world clinical environments.

items.title: Design and Evaluation of an Artificial Intelligence–Based Model for Predicting Twelfth-Grade Students’ Mathematics Performance Based on Individual, Educational, and Learning Technology Factors
items.abstract: Purpose: This study aimed to design and evaluate an artificial intelligence–based model for predicting the mathematics performance of twelfth-grade experimental sciences students based on individual, educational, and learning technology factors. Methods and Materials: This applied, quantitative, cross-sectional, and predictive study was conducted among twelfth-grade experimental sciences students in Isfahan, Iran. A total of 187 questionnaires were distributed, and after removing incomplete, inconsistent, and invalid records, data from 84 students were retained for analysis. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire assessing individual factors, educational conditions, and learning technology variables, together with students’ recorded mathematics scores. The dataset was divided into training and testing subsets, and repeated five-fold cross-validation was used for internal model development. Multiple linear regression, ridge regression, lasso regression, elastic net regression, decision tree regression, random forest regression, gradient boosting regression, and support vector regression were compared. Model performance was evaluated using mean absolute error, root mean squared error, and the coefficient of determination. Findings: Previous mathematics achievement had the strongest positive correlation with current mathematics performance, followed by mathematics self-efficacy, study regularity, academic motivation, teacher feedback, instructional quality, and educational use of learning technologies. Test anxiety and digital distraction were negatively associated with mathematics performance. Among the evaluated algorithms, gradient boosting regression achieved the best predictive performance, with a test-set mean absolute error of 0.93, root mean squared error of 1.26, and coefficient of determination of .72. Previous mathematics achievement, mathematics self-efficacy, study regularity, teacher feedback, educational use of learning technologies, test anxiety, and instructional quality were the most influential predictors. Adding educational factors increased explained variance from .54 to .65, while including learning technology factors further increased it to .72. Conclusion: The findings indicate that mathematics performance can be predicted with acceptable accuracy by integrating students’ prior achievement, psychological and behavioral characteristics, instructional experiences, and learning technology use within an interpretable artificial intelligence model.

items.title: Design and manufacture of a face shield for healthcare personnel and vulnerable populations based on frugal design principles
items.abstract: This paper presents the engineering design and manufacturing development of a low-cost face shield based on frugal design principles. The design process included conceptual design, detailed design, prototyping, and design-for-manufacture refinements. The manufacturing costs of the processes required to produce the final face shield were estimated, yielding an approximate unit cost of USD 1.36, excluding the initial injection mould tooling investment. The design supports large-scale manufacturing, with the mould intended for production volumes exceeding 50,000 units, although the project production requirement was 5,000 units. The study provides a preliminary engineering assessment focused on design, manufacturability, and cost estimation. Quantitative ergonomic, mechanical, optical, and protective-performance testing was beyond its scope.

items.title: Designing an Artificial Intelligence–Based Cognitive Empowerment Package to Enhance Entrepreneurial Skills in Gifted and Creative Adolescents
items.abstract: Purpose: This study aimed to design an artificial intelligence–based cognitive empowerment package for enhancing entrepreneurial skills in gifted and creative adolescents through the qualitative identification and integration of relevant cognitive, psychological, motivational, interpersonal, and technological components. Methods and Materials: The study employed a qualitative exploratory-developmental design. Data were obtained through an analytical review of relevant literature, examination of previous student entrepreneurship workshop experiences, and semi-structured interviews with students, mentors, workshop facilitators, and accelerator managers selected through purposive sampling. Data collection continued until conceptual saturation was achieved. Interview transcripts, field observations, documentary evidence, and analytical notes were examined using thematic analysis. Findings: The qualitative analysis indicated that sustained entrepreneurial action among gifted and creative adolescents depends on a multidimensional configuration of entrepreneurial intention and identity, self-efficacy, opportunity recognition and problem identification, executive functioning, tolerance of ambiguity, applied creativity, fear of failure and perfectionism, intrinsic motivation and psychological ownership, teamwork and psychological safety, proactive agency, resilience, future orientation, and reflective readiness to use artificial intelligence. The findings further suggested that entrepreneurial difficulties differ across adolescents and therefore require profile-based rather than uniform intervention. Integration of the themes resulted in a six-session package encompassing profile awareness and goal setting, problem identification and value creation, conversion of ideas into action plans, presentation and feedback utilization, teamwork and agency, and final presentation with a continuation plan. Conclusion: The findings suggest that entrepreneurial empowerment in gifted and creative adolescents should extend beyond creativity and business knowledge by strengthening the cognitive and psychological capacities required to transform ideas into sustained action, while using artificial intelligence as a supervised reflective and personalized learning support rather than as a substitute for adolescent judgment and agency.

items.title: Designing and Explaining an Entrepreneurship Model for Artificial Intelligence–Based Businesses
items.abstract: The primary objective of the present study was to design and explain an entrepreneurship model for artificial intelligence–based businesses, with a focus on the information and communications technology and computer software industries in knowledge-based companies located in Tehran Province. In terms of purpose, the study was applied, and in terms of approach, it was a qualitative study employing a sequential exploratory design. In the qualitative phase, grounded theory was applied using the systematic approach to identify and conceptualize the dimensions, components, and relationships among the variables affecting AI-based entrepreneurship. The qualitative research field consisted of senior and middle managers, specialists, experts, and experienced employees working in the information and communications technology and computer software industries of knowledge-based companies in Tehran Province. Participants were selected through purposive sampling, which continued until theoretical saturation was reached. Qualitative data were collected through semi-structured interviews and analyzed using MAXQDA 2024. To enhance the credibility and trustworthiness of the data, triangulation and Lincoln and Guba’s criteria, including credibility, transferability, dependability, and confirmability, were employed. The findings indicated that the entrepreneurship model for AI-based businesses consists of an interconnected set of causal conditions, contextual conditions, intervening conditions, strategies, and consequences. The causal conditions included factors such as market needs and technological gaps, entrepreneurial opportunity recognition, and customers’ digital preferences, all of which played a fundamental role in the formation of AI-based entrepreneurship. The contextual conditions included the need to establish a knowledge-based ecosystem, policymaking and regulations, financial capabilities and initial investment, advanced technological capacities, specialized human capital, team competencies, and intraorganizational collaboration. Intervening conditions, including legal and regulatory constraints associated with sensitive data and cybersecurity, as well as economic restrictions and sanctions, were also found to affect the development of entrepreneurship. According to the findings, the key strategies were the development of strategic collaborations, product development and upgrading, digital marketing and market penetration, and human capital empowerment. Finally, the consequences of implementing the model included economic and financial maturity, the development of technological authority, social and employment effects, digital transformation in upstream industries, and software export development.

items.title: Development of a Deep Learning Model Integrating Computed Tomography Images and Blood Data for the Diagnosis of Acute Cholecystitis
items.abstract: Abstract Background In this study, we aimed to develop and evaluate an artificial intelligence-based diagnostic model for the diagnosis of acute cholecystitis (AC) using non-contrast CT images and clinical data. Methods This retrospective study included 197 patients (100 AC, 97 non-AC) treated between January 2016 and December 2025 at a single center. Patients were randomly divided into training (n = 139) and test (n = 58) datasets. Three models were constructed: an imaging-based deep learning model, a clinical data-based machine learning model, and a hybrid machine learning model integrating deep learning-derived imaging features with clinical data. CT images were preprocessed, and gallbladder regions were segmented. Clinical variables included white blood cell counts and levels of C-reactive protein and liver function markers. Model performance was evaluated using accuracy, precision, recall, specificity, F1 score, and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). Statistical comparisons were performed using Welch's t-test and Chi-square test. Results The imaging-based model achieved accuracy 0.741, precision 0.703, recall 0.867, specificity 0.607, F1 score 0.776, and AUC 0.863. The blood-based model achieved accuracy 0.914, precision 0.931, recall 0.900, specificity 0.929, F1 score 0.915, and AUC 0.946. The hybrid model showed the highest performance, with accuracy 0.931, precision 0.882, recall 1.000, specificity 0.857, F1 score 0.938, and AUC 0.996. Conclusions A hybrid model integrating CT imaging and clinical data improved diagnostic performance for AC compared with single-modality models.

items.title: Development of dual-function ergonomically smart settee for academic staff office uses
items.abstract: This study focused on developing a Dual-Function Ergonomically Smart Settee (D-FESS) tailored for academic offices in the Faculty of Technology, University of Ibadan, Nigeria. The goal was to optimize office space use and support casual, intermittent rest to reduce stress among academic staff. A preliminary survey was conducted from November 2023 to March 2024, involving 33 purposively selected academic staff. Data were gathered using structured questionnaires, oral interviews, direct office assessments and anthropometric measurements. Results showed that academics spend 5 to 16 hours daily in their offices, with about 70% of this time seated, indicating a sedentary work pattern. A majority (96%) reported experiencing work-related stress and expressed a need for a D-FESS. Average office space was 4.5 m by 4.3 m, with some unused space available for new furniture. Anthropometric data were collected and the 95th percentile values were used to design and fabricate a D-FESS suitable for one academic office. The study established the need for ergonomic, space-efficient furniture like D-FESS to enhance comfort and productivity in academic environments.

items.title: DEVELOPMENT OF THE DIGITAL ECONOMY IN UZBEKISTAN: INSTITUTIONAL FRAMEWORK, TECHNOLOGICAL TRANSFORMATION AND ECONOMIC EFFECTS
items.abstract: The rapid development of digital technologies is transforming modern economies by creating new mechanisms of production, distribution, consumption, and public administration. This article examines the theoretical foundations and current trends of the digital economy, focusing on the experience of the Republic of Uzbekistan. Particular attention is given to the "Digital Uzbekistan – 2030" strategy, digital infrastructure, e-government, digital finance, e-commerce, the IT sector, and human capital development. The study applies systematic, comparative, and institutional approaches, as well as the analysis of statistical and regulatory information. The findings show that Uzbekistan has established important institutional and technological foundations for digital transformation. However, challenges remain, including the digital divide, a shortage of qualified specialists, cybersecurity risks, unequal regional access to digital infrastructure, and regulatory gaps. The study proposes strengthening digital infrastructure, developing digital skills, expanding the application of artificial intelligence and big data, supporting digital entrepreneurship, and promoting international digital integration. items.title: Didactic potential and limitations of generative artificial intelligence in teaching Russian
items.abstract: This article examines the didactic potential and limitations of generative artificial intelligence in teaching Russian as a foreign language. Its aim is to classify instructional scenarios and identify conditions for pedagogically appropriate implementation. The materials include scholarly and methodological publications, UNESCO guidance, and illustrative activities designed to develop grammatical, lexical, and communicative competence. The study employs literature analysis, comparison of teaching approaches, and qualitative evaluation of learning situations. Discussed applications include exercises on case government and verb forms, simulated dialogues, preliminary feedback on written responses, and support for independent practice. Potential limitations include inaccurate explanations, stylistically inappropriate suggestions, insufficient sensitivity to cultural context, and reduced learner autonomy. It also emphasizes personal data protection and expert review of automatically generated recommendations. The research is theoretical and methodological; no classroom experiment or measured learning outcomes are reported. The framework combines digital assistance, teacher guidance, and independent practice. Future classroom validation remains necessary.

items.title: Digital transformation is associated with lower ecological footprint across developed and developing economies
items.abstract: The rapid expansion of the digital economy is transforming global production and consumption systems, yet its environmental implications remain insufficiently understood. This study examines the relationship between the Digital Economy Index (DEI) and ecological footprint (EF) across 77 developed and developing countries from 2001 to 2020. An integrated empirical framework combining fixed-effects and System GMM estimation with machine learning techniques, Random Forest (RF), and Support Vector Machine (SVM), is employed to provide complementary econometric and predictive evidence. Econometric results show that digitalization significantly reduces EF on average, with stronger environmental benefits observed in developed economies. Moderation analysis reveals that industrialization and trade openness weaken these environmental benefits, whereas artificial intelligence, ICT development, and renewable energy transitions strengthen them. The transmission-channel analysis further suggests that environmental technological innovation and changes in the energy structure may represent potential pathways linking digitalization to environmental outcomes. The machine learning analysis provides complementary predictive evidence and identifies a nonlinear pattern in the DEI–EF relationship, potentially exhibiting an inverted U-shape in which ecological pressure increases at earlier stages of digitalization but declines at more advanced stages. RF and SVM achieve predictive accuracies of 94% and 80%, respectively. Overall, the findings indicate that digitalization is not inherently green and that its environmental benefits depend on the stage of digital development and broader structural and technological conditions, highlighting the importance of clean energy integration and sustainable digital transformation.

items.title: Digitalisation, Older Workers, Social Inequalities, and Health in Portugal
items.abstract: In a context of demographic ageing and accelerating digital transformation, understanding the impact of digitalisation on older workers is increasingly relevant. This chapter explores how these shifts shape social and health inequalities among older workers in Portugal. Using national and European data, it outlines trends in employment, education, and health for workers aged 55 and over and examines the growing digital divide between generations. It also identifies policy initiatives and best practices that promote digital inclusion and support older adults’ participation in the workforce. Special attention is given to the effects of remote work, digital skills gaps, and workplace ergonomics. The chapter concludes with recommendations for inclusive policies that foster active ageing, reduce disparities, and ensure older workers remain valued in a digital society.

items.title: Digitalization of the International Legal Sphere: Systemic Challenges And Prospects for the Evolution of International Law
items.abstract: This article examines the digital transformation of international law as a multidimensional process of rethinking traditional mechanisms of international interaction. It is argued that the penetration of digital technologies into the sphere of international legal regulation leads not only to the emergence of new objects of legal protection but also to the transformation of established approaches to determining state jurisdiction, enforcing international responsibility, and ensuring compliance with international obligations. The paper identifies the key challenges of the digital age for international law, including the fragmentation of international regulation of the digital environment, the asymmetry of states’ technological capabilities, the complexity of establishing liability for cross-border digital offenses, and the need to harmonize cybersecurity requirements with international human rights standards. The study emphasizes that the effectiveness of international legal regulation increasingly depends on the ability of international institutions and states to ensure the interaction of universal legal principles with flexible mechanisms for responding to technological risks without undermining guarantees of human rights, state sovereignty, and international security. Promising directions for legal development are outlined, including the improvement of international standards for digital governance, the formation of coordinated approaches to international legal liability for the use of digital technologies, the strengthening of international cooperation in the field of cybersecurity, and the development of regulatory mechanisms to oversee the use of artificial intelligence. The paper demonstrates the advisability of transitioning from a piecemeal response to individual technological threats to a systematic model of international legal regulation based on the principles of coherence and respect for fundamental human rights. It is concluded that the digital transformation of international law represents not only a technology-driven challenge but also an opportunity to renew its normative potential, institutional capacity, and instruments for ensuring the international legal order in the context of global digital interdependence.

items.title: Does Informal Digital Learning of English Work Through Feelings or Through Traits? A Three-Level Meta-Analysis of Affective and Individual-Difference Pathways
items.abstract: Informal digital learning of English (IDLE) — learners' self-organized engagement with English through short videos, social media, streaming, gaming, and generative AI outside the classroom — has accumulated a large body of empirical research over the past decade, yet its affective and individual-difference correlates have never been quantitatively synthesized. Existing meta-analyses address only overall effects on achievement, and narrative reviews of emotion and individual-difference variables have pooled no effect sizes. This preregistration reports a three-level meta-analysis that (1) estimates the strength of association between IDLE and positive emotions, negative emotions, and individual-difference variables; (2) tests whether the association with positive emotions is stronger than that with negative emotions, as predicted by broaden-and-build and control-value theories; and (3) explores whether the affective pathway is conditional on trait-like individual differences. Ten sources (Web of Science, ERIC, PsycINFO, OpenAlex, ScienceDirect, Taylor & Francis, Semantic Scholar, Google Scholar, CNKI, Scopus) will be searched for correlational studies published from 2014 onward. Effect sizes (Pearson's r, Fisher's z-transformed) will be modeled with three-level random-effects models cross-validated by cluster-robust variance estimation, with seven prespecified moderators and publication-bias correction (PET-PEESE). Expected outcomes are the first preregistered, effect-size-level synthesis of the IDLE–affect/individual-difference literature, clarifying whether IDLE works through feelings or through traits.

items.title: Draft International Treaty on Artificial Intelligence Governance: Model Draft (Version 1.3, complete with Annexes I–VII)
items.abstract: This is a model draft of an international treaty on artificial intelligence governance. It is not a binding instrument and has not been adopted, signed or ratified by any State. The draft is built around human dignity, human agency and the protection of persons in vulnerable situations; effective human control and an obligation of prior constraint (evaluation of an action before it is generated or takes external effect, with three evaluation "gates" for dignity, ethics and necessity/irreversibility, and a duty to hold and escalate to a human); obligations of developers, providers and deployers; transparency, record-keeping and preservation of evidence; independent audit and technical verification; individual rights to know, to human review, to object and to an effective remedy, with protection of complainants and whistleblowers; and international oversight bodies, cooperation and dispute settlement. The full texts of Annexes I to VII (terms, risk classification and objects of evaluation; the Dignity, Ethics and Necessity Gates; hold, human escalation and record-keeping requirements; the prior constraint mechanism; and independent verification and technical verification standards) are included in draft form and remain subject to the drafting reservations; figures and thresholds are left in square brackets for later determination. The final pages list the drafting reservations and matters requiring legal and technical consideration before any diplomatic negotiation. Comments and suggestions are welcome. AI use statement: Artificial intelligence tools were used to assist in drafting, translating and editing this document and its annexes. The author directed the content, reviewed it, and is responsible for the final text.

items.title: Dynamic PGA: Progressive Boundary Formation
items.abstract: Dynamic PGA: Progressive Boundary Formation extends the Dynamic Personalized Guidance Architecture (Dynamic PGA) framework by examining how personalization, trust, human agency, and boundaries should develop together in adaptive AI experiences. As AI systems become increasingly personalized, usefulness depends not only on what an AI system learns about an individual, but also on understanding what information should not be disclosed, reused, inferred, or carried into another context. This paper introduces Progressive Boundary Formation as a human-centered process through which individuals can recognize, communicate, test, and revise personal, relational, professional, and organizational boundaries as their interaction with AI develops. The framework considers the transition from private AI-assisted exploration to consequential human action, including communication, publication, professional activity, and interactions involving other people. It proposes that boundary awareness should develop alongside personalization and trust rather than appearing only as a static privacy setting or late-stage safeguard. Progressive Boundary Formation is presented as a conceptual extension of Dynamic PGA and its broader goal of creating AI experiences that adapt with the human while preserving human judgment, agency, relationships, and appropriate boundaries. items.title: EFL Students’ Experiences with AI-Powered Language Learning Tools: Implications for Learner-Centered Intelligent Tutoring Systems
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has become increasingly integrated into English language learning through tools that provide adaptive learning, automated feedback, and personalized support. Although previous studies have examined the educational benefits of AI-powered tools, relatively little is known about how English as a Foreign Language (EFL) students experience these technologies and how their perspectives can inform the design of learner-centered Intelligent Tutoring Systems (ITS). This study explored EFL students’ experiences, perceived benefits, challenges, and expectations regarding AI-powered tools for English language learning. A qualitative research design was adopted using semi-structured interviews with nine Vietnamese university EFL students, and the data were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis. The findings showed that participants experienced AI-powered language learning tools as adaptive, feedback-oriented, and engaging. They particularly valued immediate feedback, flexible learning opportunities, and gamified features, which they associated with greater confidence, motivation, and learner autonomy. At the same time, participants expressed concerns about over-reliance on AI, the contextual and cultural appropriateness of AI-generated feedback, and data privacy and security. Participants also envisioned future ITS as more conversational, personalized, and culturally responsive systems that could better address individual learning needs. Overall, the findings suggest that participants viewed AI as a valuable learning support while emphasizing the importance of independent learning, teacher guidance, and contextual relevance. The study offers preliminary design implications for learner-centered ITS by highlighting the importance of incorporating learners’ experiences and expectations into future AI-supported language learning systems.

items.title: Elemental potential of streets: A self-organizing model of the geological conditions of the province of Quebec using investigative and generative AI
items.abstract: Current urban planning treats the subsurface as a passive solid or void, constrained by a “needs to resources” paradigm that marginalizes geological knowledge. Standard mapping methodologies, particularly those using the Analytic Hierarchy Process, rely on manual expert solicitation, which is logistically burdensome and prone to cognitive blind spots. This research proposes a theoretical shift from target-oriented systems to an obstacle-oriented framework. Designating the street segment as the fundamental unit of analysis across the province of Québec, this research presents a prototype that implements a static knowledge-retrieval pipeline where a Large Language Model serves as an informational model for preliminary planning, translating hydrogeological constraints into qualitative assessments. These textual descriptions are then encoded into a continuous partition spectrum using a one-dimensional self-organizing map. The prototype demonstrates high computational robustness in standardizing qualitative data, successfully mapping the geological dichotomy between the stable crystalline basement of the Canadian Shield and the conflict-prone sedimentary basins of the St. Lawrence Lowlands. By converting qualitative data into relational contextual numbers, the model identifies latent synergies without predefined target functions. The article concludes that this pre-specific modeling approach validates the utility of artificial intelligence in mitigating cognitive blind spots, demonstrating how computational models can complement human engineering by repositioning geological insights at the very beginning of the urban design process. By establishing a topos of communication capable of circulating around the inherent opacity of the geological volume, this method offers a scalable instrument for sustainable underground urbanism that treats the earth not as an anecdotal resource, but as an active constituent of the built environment.

items.title: Enabling artificial intelligence in entrepreneurship: Implications for startup creation in higher education
items.abstract: The digital transformation has reshaped entrepreneurship, with the emergence of artificial intelligence (AI) as a powerful enabler of innovation and startup creation. However, higher education institutions face challenges integrating AI into entrepreneurship education curriculum, limiting students’ ability to fully harness its potential. This study aimed to determine and explore entrepreneurship students’ challenges in using AI for startup development, assess the competencies they gain in innovating business ideas, and analyze how these challenges affect competencies using structural equation modeling (SEM). Employing an convergent mixed-method design, the study surveyed 114 third- and fourth-year BS Entrepreneurship students and conducted interviews to faculty and business plan implementers. Quantitative data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and SEM, while qualitative data underwent thematic analysis for triangulation. Findings revealed that students face significant challenges in opportunity identification, decision-making, performance execution, education and learning, and research application. The key barriers highlight was market understanding, lack of AI literacy, limited mentorship, and insufficient curriculum integration. Despite these, students reported gaining competencies in opportunity recognition, customer targeting, data-informed decision-making, and entrepreneurial communication using AI tools. However, critical thinking, problem-solving, and prototyping skills remained underdeveloped. SEM results indicated that challenges in education, opportunity identification, and decision-making significantly constrained entrepreneurial competencies. The study implies the need for higher education to reform curricula by embedding AI-focused modules, case-based projects, mentorship opportunities, and innovation hubs. Strengthening AI-driven entrepreneurship education will equip students with the competencies required for sustainable startup creation in the digital economy.

items.title: Enabling artificial intelligence in entrepreneurship: Implications for startup creation in higher education
items.abstract: The digital transformation has reshaped entrepreneurship, with the emergence of artificial intelligence (AI) as a powerful enabler of innovation and startup creation. However, higher education institutions face challenges integrating AI into entrepreneurship education curriculum, limiting students’ ability to fully harness its potential. This study aimed to determine and explore entrepreneurship students’ challenges in using AI for startup development, assess the competencies they gain in innovating business ideas, and analyze how these challenges affect competencies using structural equation modeling (SEM). Employing an convergent mixed-method design, the study surveyed 114 third- and fourth-year BS Entrepreneurship students and conducted interviews to faculty and business plan implementers. Quantitative data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and SEM, while qualitative data underwent thematic analysis for triangulation. Findings revealed that students face significant challenges in opportunity identification, decision-making, performance execution, education and learning, and research application. The key barriers highlight was market understanding, lack of AI literacy, limited mentorship, and insufficient curriculum integration. Despite these, students reported gaining competencies in opportunity recognition, customer targeting, data-informed decision-making, and entrepreneurial communication using AI tools. However, critical thinking, problem-solving, and prototyping skills remained underdeveloped. SEM results indicated that challenges in education, opportunity identification, and decision-making significantly constrained entrepreneurial competencies. The study implies the need for higher education to reform curricula by embedding AI-focused modules, case-based projects, mentorship opportunities, and innovation hubs. Strengthening AI-driven entrepreneurship education will equip students with the competencies required for sustainable startup creation in the digital economy.

items.title: Enhancing Clinical Reasoning Development: An AI-Assisted Learning Framework for Unstructured Problem-Solving in Medical Education
items.abstract: Abstract Background Clinical reasoning for unstructured problems—those lacking clearly defined initial conditions, standard protocols, or singular correct solutions—remains a persistent challenge in medical education. While artificial intelligence (AI) tools have shown promise in structured knowledge tasks, their integration into frameworks designed for unstructured clinical reasoning remains underexplored. Methods A systems thinking assessment framework was adapted for medical education and validated through expert review and inter-rater reliability testing (ICC = 0.801, 95% CI: 0.725–0.866). Fifty-five medical students were randomly assigned to three groups: an AI-assisted learning group (AIL, n = 18) using ChatGPT 4.0 as a guided reasoning aid, a conventional learning group (CL, n = 18) using textbooks and non-AI online resources, and a manual group (MG, n = 19) without any supplementary tools. All participants responded to the same unstructured clinical case comprising seven tasks (Q1–Q7), each scored on a 0–3 scale by five blinded raters. As an exploratory benchmark, ChatGPT 4.0 responses to the identical case were independently scored using the same framework to characterize the AI model's performance profile and limitations. Results The AIL group achieved the highest mean total score (12.11 ± 1.78), significantly outperforming the CL group (8.94 ± 1.08, p < 0.0001) and the MG (9.97 ± 2.37, p < 0.01). Significant advantages were observed in Q2 (information needs), Q5 (scenario development), Q6 (challenges), and Q7 (unintended consequences). Subgroup analysis revealed no significant interaction between learning tools and baseline academic performance (F = 0.213, p = 0.930, η² = 0.018), suggesting consistent benefits across GPA levels. The ChatGPT 4.0 benchmark produced uniformly identical scores (total score 16.5 across all trials), revealing characteristic limitations in response variability and template dependency. Conclusions An AI-assisted learning framework grounded in a validated systems thinking assessment tool can enhance medical students' clinical reasoning for unstructured problems, with effects that appear independent of baseline academic performance. The ChatGPT benchmark highlights both the capabilities and the rigidities of current AI models, underscoring the need for hybrid human–AI collaboration rather than AI substitution in clinical reasoning education. items.title: Entrepreneurial Orientation and Startup Business Sustainability: The Mediating Role of the Quality of Artificial Intelligence Utilization
items.abstract: The Indonesian startup ecosystem has experienced growing funding pressures and rising demands for operational efficiency, making business sustainability an increasingly important priority. Therefore, this study aims to examine the effect of entrepreneurial orientation on business sustainability, with the quality of Artificial Intelligence (AI) utilization serving as a mediator among startup employees in Greater Jakarta and Bandung. Using a causal quantitative design, the study surveyed 107 respondents selected through purposive sampling. Data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling in SmartPLS 4, and the obtained results showed that entrepreneurial orientation positively affected both business sustainability (β=0.380; p<0.001) and the quality of AI utilization (β=0.603; p<0.001). The quality of AI utilization was also observed to positively affect business sustainability (β=0.376; p=0.001). Accordingly, the obtained indirect effect of 0.227 (p=0.001) confirms partial mediation, with a VAF of 37.4%. These findings expand the Resource-Based View (RBV) by positioning entrepreneurial orientation as a strategic capability and the quality of AI utilization as a technological-operational capability that transforms the orientation into business efficiency, productivity, adaptability, and resilience. Practically, startups need to integrate an entrepreneurial culture, AI literacy, data governance, infrastructure support, and AI impact evaluation into respective business processes.

items.title: ESP Students’ Reading Motivation at a Vietnamese University: An Explanatory Sequential Mixed-Methods Study
items.abstract: Reading proficiency is central to academic success in English for Specific Purposes (ESP) settings, yet motivation to read discipline-specific texts remains underexplored among non-English majors in Vietnam. Grounded in Self-Determination Theory and the Reading Motivation Questionnaire for English as a Foreign Language (RMQ-EFL), this study investigated the reading motivation of 416 Economic Law students enrolled in a compulsory “English for Economic Law” course at a public university in Ho Chi Minh City. The RMQ-EFL framework specifies five factors: three intrinsic (reading efficacy, reading enjoyment, involvement) and two extrinsic (recognition, compliance). An explanatory sequential mixed-methods design was employed, combining a quantitative survey (N = 416) with follow-up semi-structured interviews (N = 20) to explain the survey patterns. Descriptive statistics, paired-samples t-tests, and independent-samples t-tests were conducted in SPSS 27, and the interview data were analyzed thematically. The results revealed that extrinsic motivation significantly exceeded intrinsic motivation, with compliance recording the highest mean and reading efficacy the lowest. No statistically significant differences emerged between male and female students on either intrinsic or extrinsic motivation. The qualitative findings clarified these patterns: students’ strong compliance orientation reflected Vietnamese cultural values emphasizing respect for authority, diligence, and academic responsibility, along with grade- and graduation-related pressures, whereas their low reading efficacy stemmed from difficulties with specialized legal vocabulary and limited confidence in comprehending complex legal texts. Intrinsic engagement nonetheless emerged when reading materials were perceived as personally relevant or career-oriented. These findings suggest that ESP instruction should build on students’ existing compliance while fostering more autonomous motivation through career-relevant reading materials, systematic vocabulary support, and strategy-based instruction. The study contributes empirical evidence on how cultural and institutional contexts shape ESP reading motivation in Asian higher education.

items.title: Ethical and Policy Challenges in Implementing Artificial Intelligence in Health Care System
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence, as an advanced and emerging technology, has brought about significant transformations in healthcare in recent years. By leveraging complex algorithms and big data analytics, this technology facilitates improved diagnostic accuracy, predictive disease modeling, and personalized treatment approaches. This paper explores various applications of artificial intelligence within healthcare systems, including disease diagnosis and treatment, resource management, and enhancement of patient care. Additionally, the study analyzes challenges related to the adoption of AI technologies such as ethical concerns, patient privacy protection, and technical and infrastructural limitations. The importance of developing effective policies and standards, training specialized human resources, and increasing the acceptance of novel technologies within the healthcare community are also highlighted as essential prerequisites for successful implementation. The findings demonstrate that with proper management of associated challenges and optimal utilization, artificial intelligence can serve as a transformative force, fostering new prospects for improving healthcare quality and community health outcomes.

items.title: ETHICAL AND REGULATORY COMPLIANCE IN THE EVALUATION OF CLINICAL RESEARCH INVOLVING ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN SUB SAHARAN AFRICA
items.abstract: In recent years, the use of artificial intelligence (AI) in research involving human participants has gained popularity in clinical and biomedical research domains, more so in advance economies than in low medium income countries (LMIC) like Cameroon. AI is transformative in its ability to perform faster repetitive tasks, analyze large amounts of data, and potentially leading to enhance clinical research decision-making. As with all research involving human participants, research using AI should be in compliance with ethical principles and subject to regulatory guidelines for better protection of volunteering research participants. The use of AI in research involving human participants presents new ethical and regulatory challenges, including those related to privacy and data confidentiality, transparency, amplification of bias, and implications for maintaining human autonomy and oversight. Existing guidelines of most research ethics committees relating to digital health technology evaluation for human research are not up-to- date to address AI evaluation in clinical research. In view of providing a regulatory compliant structure that protects the human participant’s privacy and mitigation of bias Sub-Saharan African countries have an obligation to update their standard operating procedures to integrate aspects for evaluating AI research. There are however, a few existing guidelines from developed countries like the US and Canada that provide the ethical foundations for the use of AI in clinical research. Tools are still required to enhance the protocol review process by the research ethics committees charged with ensuring consistency, efficiency and sustainability across institutions, to reflect accepted standards of ethical research review oversight. This document aims to focus on AI contributions in clinical research, challenges and adopted guidelines for evaluation of AI-driven clinical research. This is in view of providing support for Institutional Review Boards (IRBs) and other ethics advocacy institutions with the awareness and practical friendly user steps to identify, assess, and mitigate potential risks to participants in an AI-driven research, during the ethical review process.

items.title: ETHNO PHARMACOLOGY AND THE SCIENTIFIC INTEGRATION OF TRADITIONAL MEDICINE: ADVANCING HOLISTIC AND EVIDENCE-BASED HEALTHCARE
items.abstract: Traditional medicine systems continue to serve as primary healthcare resources for a substantial proportion of the global population, particularly in low- and middle-income countries where access to modern medical infrastructure remains limited. Ethnopharmacology has emerged as a critical interdisciplinary field that systematically bridges indigenous knowledge systems with contemporary biomedical science, enabling scientific validation, standardization, and integration of traditional therapeutic practices. This comprehensive review examines the evolving role of ethnopharmacology in advancing holistic treatment paradigms through methodological innovations such as network pharmacology, systems biology, metabolomics, artificial intelligence, and multi-omics technologies. The paper critically analyzes multimodal therapeutic strategies, constitutional typing frameworks, and mind–body integration approaches embedded within traditional medicine systems. Furthermore, it evaluates current challenges related to clinical validation, quality control, regulatory harmonization, safety assessment, and ethical issues including intellectual property rights and equitable benefit-sharing. Emerging evidence suggests that traditional medicine offers promising complementary strategies for managing complex chronic and multifactorial diseases; however, rigorous interdisciplinary research, robust clinical methodologies, and culturally sensitive policy frameworks are essential for its sustainable integration into global healthcare systems. Strengthening collaborations between traditional knowledge holders and scientific communities will be pivotal in developing equitable, evidence-based, and patient-centered holistic healthcare models.

items.title: Evaluation of large language models’ responses to patient questions about avascular necrosis of the femoral head
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence chatbots are rapidly gaining popularity for acquiring health information, but the quality of responses seems to differ between platforms. This study investigated the responses of ChatGPT, Gemini, Copilot, Claude, and DeepSeek to 15 frequently asked questions regarding femoral head avascular necrosis. Each platform answered each question once, for a total of 75 responses. Four orthopedic surgeons assessed the response using the JAMA benchmark criteria, DISCERN, an adapted five-point scale of clinical accuracy, and a binary safety score. Readability was measured by Flesch reading ease score (FRES) and Flesch-Kincaid grade level (FKGL). Models were compared by using Friedman tests and Bonferroni-corrected Wilcoxon signed-rank tests. Claude ranked the highest by JAMA and DISCERN scores and that DeepSeek outperformed ChatGPT, Gemini, and Copilot in terms of DISCERN. Clinical accuracy differed significantly among the models ( p < 0.001). Claude and DeepSeek were rated higher than ChatGPT, Gemini, and Copilot, with no significant difference between Claude and DeepSeek. All responses were rated safe by all four raters. Readability performance scores of the models achieved significant differences on FRES ( p = 0.043) and FKGL ( p < 0.001) measures. The average FKGL score (10.85–13.93) was higher than the grade scores recommended for patient education information. There was heterogeneity in the platforms ability to report on aspects of transparency, information quality and clinical accuracy while consistently failing on readability. Patient comprehension was not evaluated.

items.title: Evaluative Language and Metaphor in Museum Discourse: Assessing AI-Based Analysis of the Savitsky Museum Catalogue
items.abstract: Museum catalogue texts do more than describe works of art; they also express judgements about artistic value and use figurative language to guide interpretation. This study focuses on evaluative language and metaphor in selected English-language descriptions from the I.V. Savitsky State Museum of Art of the Republic of Karakalpakstan. Four catalogue entries are examined: Caravan, Northern Lights, Houses, and The Old and the New. The analysis considers how individual expressions function in context and how evaluative meaning can overlap with metaphorical or symbolic interpretation. ChatGPT is used as an analytical tool to identify relevant expressions and explain their possible meanings. Its interpretations need to be checked against the original catalogue texts, since a plausible explanation does not necessarily mean that a classification is linguistically justified. The study also considers the difficulty of distinguishing figurative language from literal description, particularly when a phrase performs more than one function. By focusing on specific examples from museum discourse, the research explores the usefulness of AI-assisted linguistic analysis while recognising the continuing importance of careful human interpretation.

items.title: Exact Algebraic Reduction of Quantum Neural Circuits: Observable-Dependent Renormalization and Curvature-Based Reliability Control
items.abstract: This conference presentation introduces an algebraic framework for the exact reduction of quantum neural circuits through observable-dependent renormalization and geometric reliability control. The proposed approach addresses fundamental challenges in quantum machine learning, including circuit complexity, fragmented mathematical representations, training stability, and the reliability of generative models. The framework represents parameterized quantum circuits as quantum dynamical semigroups and constructs an observable-dependent symmetry subalgebra using dynamical Lie algebra closure. This construction enables the derivation of reduced effective models that preserve designated observables exactly while maintaining complete positivity and trace preservation. The presentation further investigates the geometric structure of reduced quantum models through quantum Fisher information, Berry curvature, and context-dependent attention metrics. Geometric regularization is proposed to improve training stability and address barren plateaus, while curvature-based reliability monitoring provides a mathematical approach to detecting deviations of generated outputs from learned data manifolds. The proposed methodology offers potential applications in resource-efficient quantum machine learning, hybrid quantum-classical computing, model robustness, and AI reliability. Future research directions include hardware-aware algebraic reduction, continuous-variable quantum systems, and curvature-based monitoring for trustworthy artificial intelligence.

items.title: ExpEvolve: Structuring and Reusing Experience for Open-Ended Discovery
items.abstract: Evolutionary coding agents such as AlphaEvolve are one of the notable successes in using Large Language Models (LLMs) to build AI Scientists. These agents tackle open-ended scientific problems by iteratively improving and evolving programs, leveraging the prior knowledge and reasoning capabilities of LLMs. Despite their success, mutations over programs are mostly low-level upon surface heuristics, without a persistent unit of control. In contrast, science compounds through ideas. In this work, we propose ExpEvolve, which injects idea-level extraction and control into evolution: it discovers and leverages the high-level factors from programs that explain scoring differences among different programs. We characterize theoretical conditions on when discovery with idea factors improves sample efficiency. We also build a practical framework to show that the extracted high-level idea factors are helpful for guiding exploitation from experience and exploration when discovery comes to a plateau. Across 11 open-ended mathematical tasks, ExpEvolve significantly improves the final performance and sample efficiency up to 5.0x. The improvements also transfer to 4 other LLMs and to 6 machine learning tasks from MLS-Bench. Analysis shows that ExpEvolve can discover idea-level factors to provide better exploration and exploitation for evolutionary discovery.

items.title: Facial expression recognition based on multi-scale dual-channel attention mechanism
items.abstract: In recent years, with the continuous advancement of artificial intelligence technology, the way humans interact with computers has undergone significant changes. Facial expression recognition technology for human faces has increasingly become a hot research topic in computer vision. However, traditional facial expression recognition models are based on deep neural networks, which have problems such as insufficient extraction of image details, poor generalization ability of the model, and low utilization rate of key feature information. To address these issues, in this paper, a Multi-scale Dual-channel Attention Mechanism Facial Expression Recognition Network (MDAMNet) is proposed. Firstly, a Multi-scale Feature Extraction Block with Dilated Convolution (DMFE Block) is designed, which uses ordinary convolution and dilated convolution to form different receptive fields. The model can focus on and extract feature information at different scales at the same time. Then, a Dual-channel Attention Mechanism (DAM) combining channel attention and spatial attention is designed, which can enhance the perception ability and extraction ability of key features, and effectively suppress redundant information. Finally, Focal Loss is employed to dynamically adjust the loss function, with the aim of enhancing the accuracy and stability of the system. During the experimental verification stage, experiments were conducted on three publicly available classic datasets (FER2013, CK + and JAFFE). The final accuracy rates reached 76.87%, 97.52% and 98.34% respectively, effectively demonstrating the feasibility of this method.

items.title: Factors Affecting the Adoption of Metaverse Technology Among Librarians in Federal Universities of Technology in Nigeria
items.abstract: Abstract Introduction Librarians' readiness for metaverse technology in Nigerian universities of technology is not well documented. This study aimed to assess librarians' awareness, digital skills, perceived infrastructure, organizational support, and challenges regarding metaverse technology in Federal Universities of Technology in Nigeria, and to examine the relationships between awareness and digital skills and between infrastructure and organizational support. Methods This cross-sectional survey was conducted between April and July 2026 in six Federal Universities of Technology in Nigeria. Academic librarians in these universities who agreed to participate were included, and incomplete questionnaires were excluded. Data were collected with a validated online questionnaire using four-point scales. Descriptive statistics were used with a criterion mean of 2.50, and Pearson correlation was used to test the hypotheses at a 0.05 significance level. Results A total of 103 librarians were included. Overall, 97 (94.2%) reported very high or high awareness of the metaverse concept. While 91 (88.3%) reported being able to operate metaverse access devices, 29 (28.2%) reported being able to upload library content. Reliable internet connectivity was reported by 87 (84.5%), and augmented reality devices by 27 (26.2%). Inadequate training was the most highly rated challenge, reported by 98 (95.1%). Awareness was correlated with digital skills (r = 0.49, p < 0.001), and infrastructure with organizational support (r = 0.38, p < 0.001). Conclusion Librarians appeared to be aware of metaverse technology, but their skills and resources seemed better suited to accessing virtual environments than to delivering library services within them. Introduction The metaverse refers to a persistent, shared multiuser virtual environment that merges physical reality with digital virtuality, in which users interact with one another and with digital content through avatars, supported by virtual, augmented, and mixed reality technologies [1]. The term originated in the 1992 science fiction novel Snow Crash, and the concept has since attracted substantial attention from technology companies and researchers [1,2]. In academic libraries, metaverse technologies have been applied or proposed for virtual tours, exhibitions, information literacy instruction, access to digital collections, and interaction between librarians and users [3,4]. Librarians' awareness of and readiness for metaverse technology have been examined in Thailand, the Gulf region, the United States, and Nigeria [5–8]. Factors reported to influence adoption include librarians' awareness and digital competence; the availability of devices, software, bandwidth, and electricity; and organizational support in the form of funding, training, technical assistance, and policy [9,10]. Privacy, data protection, and cybersecurity have also been identified as implementation concerns [11]. In Nigeria, studies of university libraries have reported variation in digital competencies and technological resources, and interest in metaverse applications alongside limitations in expertise, infrastructure, funding, training, and policy [8,12]. Federal Universities of Technology hold a mandate for technological education and research; however, librarians' awareness, digital skills, and perceptions of infrastructure, organizational support, and challenges relating to metaverse technology in these institutions remain insufficiently documented. This study aimed to assess librarians' awareness, digital skills, perceived infrastructure, organizational support, and challenges regarding metaverse technology in Federal Universities of Technology in Nigeria, and to examine the relationships between awareness and digital skills and between infrastructure and organizational support. Literature Review Awareness of Metaverse Technology among Librarians Proposed library applications of metaverse technology include immersive user engagement and changes to collections and reading spaces [3,13]; virtual, augmented, and mixed reality services [14]; virtual tours, simulations, tutorials, and collaborative spaces [4]; and immersive information literacy instruction [15]. From the user perspective, studies have examined willingness to patronise a metaverse academic library [16], intentions to use metaverse digital library services [17], knowledge exchange through a virtual living library [18], and information needs involving interaction, participation, and user-generated content in metaverse communities [19]. Among librarians, moderate awareness has been reported in Thailand [5] and in Nigeria, where it was accompanied by enthusiasm for adoption [12]. However, the relationship between librarians' awareness and their digital skills has not been examined in Nigerian Federal Universities of Technology. Digital Skills Possessed by Librarians for the Adoption of Metaverse Technology New professional capabilities have been described as necessary for librarians in intelligent library environments [20]. Librarians in the Gulf region have reported substantial familiarity with and interest in metaverse technology, together with barriers related to expertise and technical resources [6]. Positive views of metaverse integration have also been reported alongside gaps in technical expertise [21]. In Nigeria, digital skills have been associated with preparedness for metaverse-enabled services [12], and readiness and digital capacity have been reported to vary across universities [8]. Training has been recommended to address these gaps [4,10,22]. However, existing studies have not distinguished librarians' ability to navigate virtual environments from their ability to create content, retrieve resources, and communicate with users within them. Adequacy of Technological Infrastructure for the Adoption of Metaverse Technology Infrastructure has been identified as a factor in the adoption of metaverse technologies in academic libraries [9] and has been associated with readiness among library professionals in Pakistan [23]. Immersive library applications and scalable metaverse service models require high-capacity connectivity, and internet and infrastructure constraints have been identified as barriers to implementation [4,14]. Reviews of metaverse technologies in libraries have also highlighted implementation constraints [10,22]. In Nigeria, studies have reported uneven technological resources and limited institutional readiness [8,12]. In a related context, facilitating conditions have been associated with librarians' adoption of artificial intelligence [24]. Organizational Support Available for the Adoption of Metaverse Technology Institutional encouragement has been linked with favorable perceptions of metaverse technology among librarians [6], and leadership support has been identified as a component of readiness in Pakistan [23]. In urban libraries in the United States, overall operating expenditure and population served did not explain the application of metaverse-related technologies [7]. In Nigeria, financial and policy constraints have been reported [12]. Recommended measures include professional development [20]; phased implementation, training, and user feedback [4]; and collaboration, policy, and investment [10,22]. Challenges Affecting the Adoption of Metaverse Technology among Librarians. Reported barriers include technical, financial, and ethical concerns in Thailand [5]; connectivity, training, and service delivery [4]; resource and inclusion issues [10,22]; and costs, skills, funding, and readiness in Nigeria [12]. Professional challenges include changes to librarians' roles [20] and changes associated with the convergence of metaverse technology and artificial intelligence [25]. Ethical and security concerns have also been identified [5,22], including cybersecurity and data protection [11]. At the service level, challenges relate to community participation and ownership of information [19] and to the transfer of knowledge exchange into virtual settings [18]. items.title: Fine-Tuning IndoBERT for Detecting AI-Generated Indonesian Text to Support Academic Integrity
items.abstract: Purpose: This study develops and evaluates a fine-tuned IndoBERT model for detecting ChatGPT-generated Indonesian text, addressing the gap left by AI-generated text detection systems built primarily for English. Design/methodology/approach – The M4 Indonesian dataset (5,774 samples after preprocessing, group-split by article source identifier into 4,619 training, 577 validation, and 578 test samples to keep matched human-written and ChatGPT-generated pairs from leaking across partitions) was used as the basis of this study. A fixed 1,000-sample subset of the training partition was used to fine-tune IndoBERT for binary text classification using PyTorch and Hugging Face Transformers (learning rate 2e-5, three epochs, AdamW) and to train the support vector machine and Naïve Bayes benchmarks under identical conditions. Performance was evaluated on the full 578-sample test set using accuracy, precision, recall and F1-score. Findings: On 578 held-out test samples, IndoBERT reached 95.85% accuracy, 92.57% precision, 100% recall, and an F1-score of 0.9614 (macro F1 = 0.9582), against 97.06% for SVM and 93.08% for Naive Bayes. An exact McNemar's test found no statistically significant difference between IndoBERT and SVM (p = .324), indicating that IndoBERT's advantage under an earlier, non-grouped split largely reflected data leakage rather than a genuine architectural advantage. Research implications/limitations – The dataset is limited to the news domain and to text generated by a single model (ChatGPT); generalisation to academic text, such as student essays, and to outputs from other LLMs, such as Gemini or LLaMA, requires further validation. Originality/value – This study demonstrates that language-specific fine-tuning of IndoBERT can support academic integrity efforts in Indonesia, offering a practical and reproducible detection pipeline that can be adapted and further validated to identify ChatGPT-generated text in educational settings.

items.title: From body-data to narrative body: Reconfiguring the human body in medical discourse in the age of Artificial Intelligence
items.abstract: The rapid integration of artificial intelligence into biomedical research and clinical practice is transforming the ways in which the human body is conceptualized and represented in medical knowledge. Rather than functioning merely as descriptive tools, scientific vocabularies and research frameworks contribute to shaping epistemic models of the body. This study investigates how contemporary medical literature reproduces particular representations of the body in the context of digital medicine and artificial intelligence. Methodologically, the research combines bibliometric mapping with discourse analysis. A systematic search of the PubMed database identified 2,518 articles published between 1973 and 2025 that include references to the body and artificial intelligence. From these articles, 7,275 keywords were extracted and analysed, with 499 terms meeting the minimum occurrence threshold for co-occurrence mapping using VOSviewer. The bibliometric analysis reveals the centrality of technical concepts associated with computational modelling, including neural networks, image processing, and computational biology. Complementary discourse analysis of the articles indicates that the body is predominantly conceptualized as a biomechanical structure, an imaging object, a network of physiological sensors, or a dataset analysed through predictive algorithms. The analysis suggests that while digital medicine expands the technological capacities of healthcare, it also risks narrowing the conceptual space in which the body is understood. In this context, the integration of perspectives from medical humanities becomes increasingly important for reconnecting biomedical innovation with the lived, ethical, and narrative dimensions of human embodiment.

items.title: FROM FIQH FORMALISM TO SUBSTANTIVE WORSHIP: A SOCIO-LEGAL ANALYSIS OF AI-BASED THEMATIC QUR’ANIC LEARNING
items.abstract: This study aims to evaluate the effectiveness of Artificial Intelligence (AI)-assisted thematic Qur’anic learning through Digital Quran version 3.1 in reshaping university students’ understanding of worship from a fiqh-formalistic perspective toward a focus on substantive worship. The research used a socio-legal approach combined with the Classroom Action Research (CAR) model by Kemmis and McTaggart. Participants included 300 university students enrolled in Islamic Religious Education courses at various higher education institutions in West Java, DKI Jakarta, and Banten. Data collection involved pre-tests, post-tests, classroom observations, students’ written reflections, and documentation of learning activities. The data were examined using thematic socio-legal analysis, employing open coding, axial coding, selective coding, discourse analysis, member checking, and interpretive validation. The findings show that, before the intervention, most students already exhibited a fairly high level of ritual compliance, especially in performing obligatory prayers and fasting. However, their understanding of worship was mainly shaped by a legal-formal mindset that focused on fulfilling the necessary conditions and pillars of worship. After implementing AI-assisted thematic Qur’anic learning, significant improvements appeared in several aspects of meaningful worship, notably awareness of repentance, fear of losing Allah’s guidance, spiritual awareness, viewing prayer as a defense against indecency and wrongdoing, and recognizing the importance of steadfastness in worship. The qualitative results reveal a developing understanding that worship involves more than just ritual validity; it also includes sincerity, humility, moral growth, and social responsibility. From a socio-legal perspective, this learning process prompted a shift from a formalistic to a reflective legal mindset, though some students still maintained a traditional fiqh perspective. This study proposes a conceptual model linking AI-assisted Qur’anic exploration, reflective Qur’anic literacy, reflective legal thinking, and a focus on meaningful worship. The results suggest that integrating AI into Qur’anic education can serve as a tool for maqāṣid-oriented digital governance, strengthening a more reflective, meaningful, and public-good-centered understanding of Islamic law.

items.title: From Unimodal to Multimodal: AI-Driven Mental Health Assessment Using Linguistic, Acoustic, and Visual Cues
items.abstract: Mental health disorders, including depression, anxiety, bipolar disorder, and schizophrenia, represent a significant global health challenge due to their high prevalence and complex diagnostic requirements. Traditional assessment methods primarily rely on clinical interviews and self-reported questionnaires, which are often subjective, time-consuming, and unsuitable for continuous or large-scale monitoring. In recent years, advances in artificial intelligence (AI) have enabled the development of multimodal mental health assessment systems that integrate diverse behavioral and physiological signals such as speech, text, facial expressions, and biosignals. This paper presents a systematic review of eight influential studies that employ multimodal machine learning and deep learning techniques for mental health analysis. The reviewed works are critically analyzed based on the datasets utilized, model architectures, multimodal fusion strategies, and evaluation metrics. Comparative findings demonstrate that multimodal approaches consistently outperform unimodal systems, offering improved accuracy, robustness, and generalization across various mental health conditions. Despite these encouraging outcomes, several challenges remain, including limited availability of high-quality labeled data, lack of model interpretability, insufficient clinical validation, and ethical concerns related to privacy and real-world deployment. This review identifies key research gaps and highlights future directions aimed at developing reliable, explainable, and ethically responsible AI-driven systems to support mental healthcare assessment and intervention

items.title: Gendered algorithms within the politics of inclusion in Chinese gaming: a feminist critique of Identity V
items.abstract: This article examines how gender inclusion and inequality coexist in Identity V, a Chinese asymmetrical survival-horror game promoted as gender-inclusive. Combining critical play analysis, participant observation, and eighteen interviews with ten women working across China’s game industry, I trace gender across gameplay, player communities, and production. I argue that avatar design, ranking and matchmaking, monetization, and moderation reproduce masculine-coded forms of competition while positioning women unevenly as players, consumers, and creators. These patterns emerge within workplace hierarchies, market pressures, and state regulation shaped by the intertwined legacies of colonialism, state socialism, market reform, and nationalist gender politics. Yet women also negotiate these constraints through collective practices: players share strategies against harassment, build support networks, and reinterpret gender-conscious design, while practitioners exchange knowledge, refer one another to jobs, mentor newcomers, and make leadership more imaginable. Combining feminist game studies, critical information studies, and feminist ethics of care, the article treats algorithms as sociotechnical infrastructures rather than neutral code. It advances a situated feminist critique of Chinese gaming that moves beyond representation to ask who designs, maintains, and reshapes the systems that govern play.

items.title: Generative AI and Composing Strategies Employed by EFL Writers: Is AI a Double-edged Sword?
items.abstract: The integration of AI tools like ChatGPT in language education presents both opportunities and challenges. This mixed-methods study examined the impact of AI on composing strategies and writing performance among 87 upper-intermediate Iranian EFL learners, randomly assigned to a traditional group (n=43) and an AI group (n=44). Both groups completed IELTS Writing Task 2 as pre- and post-tests; the AI group used ChatGPT during the post-test. Concurrent think-aloud protocols, supported by training and video demonstrations, were used to analyze writing strategies, while reflective journals provided qualitative insights. Results showed the AI group achieved significantly higher post-test scores but employed fewer cognitive, rhetorical, metacognitive, communicative, and socio-affective writing strategies, indicating reduced strategic engagement. Thematic analysis revealed learners’ ambivalence: they valued AI for efficiency and personalized feedback but expressed concerns about authenticity, creativity, equity, and academic integrity. The findings suggest that while AI can enhance writing performance, over-reliance may hinder critical skill development. The study advocates for critical AI literacy, emphasizing scaffolded, ethical AI integration aligned with Vygotskian principles. Educators should prioritize personal voice, originality, and higher-order thinking to ensure AI supports, rather than substitutes, the writing process.

items.title: Generative AI in ESG Reporting: A Case Study and Process Framework
items.abstract: ABSTRACT The emergence of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is found to have a remarkable impact on environmental, social, and governance (ESG) reporting. Although there is abundant literature on ESG reporting, very few studies have examined the adoption of GenAI in ESG reporting. As a result, this study examines how companies can use GenAI to generate value in ESG reporting. We obtain the following three findings that we articulate in this paper: (i) GenAI drives digital innovation in ESG reporting via automated data extraction, accelerated analytics, and dynamic reporting; (ii) GenAI‐powered platforms enhance stakeholder engagement by integrating diverse data sources and improving information accessibility; and (iii) organizations encounter significant challenges in data governance and human‐AI collaboration. We also propose a framework for adopting GenAI in digital ESG platforms.

items.title: Generative AI in Korean Language Learning: A Scoping Review
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is increasingly being integrated into language education, yet evidence concerning its use in Korean language learning remains fragmented. This scoping review examines the emerging research on GenAI and related artificial intelligence applications in Korean language learning, with particular attention to pedagogical affordances, language skills, learner agency, and Korean-specific linguistic and pragmatic characteristics. Following a scoping review framework, relevant literature was identified and screened across major international and Korean academic databases. The final corpus comprised 56 sources, including direct studies of GenAI in Korean language learning, earlier Korean AI and chatbot research, broader research on GenAI in second and foreign language education, and conceptual, ethical, and policy-oriented studies. The findings indicate that existing Korean-language research is concentrated primarily on writing, prompt use, learner perceptions, and university-level instruction, while evidence concerning speaking, listening, reading, and sustained classroom implementation remains comparatively limited. The review further identifies Korean-specific challenges involving honorifics, speech-level selection, contextual appropriateness, and discourse management, which may not be adequately addressed by general-purpose GenAI systems. Across the literature, effective use of GenAI appears to depend on instructional design, learner agency, human mediation, and responsible assessment rather than technology alone. The review concludes by identifying research priorities for empirically validating GenAI-supported Korean language pedagogy and developing context-sensitive, ethically responsible approaches to its integration.
