items.title: GIS-Based Landslide Susceptibility Mapping Using the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) in Batang Kali, Selangor, Malaysia
items.abstract: Landslides are a prevalent environmental risk in Malaysia, occurring mainly in hilly and tropical locations, often during the optimum time for heavy downpours. This study aims to assess the landslide susceptibility in Batang Kali, Selangor, Malaysia, utilizing the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) based on Geographic Information Systems (GIS). Based on historical records, aerial image interpretation, and remote sensing data, in combination with field verification, a landslide database of 46 identified landslide locations was produced. Sixteen influential factors, including various topographic, hydrological, environmental, and human factors, were selected for landslide susceptibility modeling. The landslide susceptibility map was created using weighted overlay analysis and classified into five levels of susceptibility, ranging from very low to very high. The resulting susceptibility map shows that 14.68% of the study area belongs to the very low susceptibility class, while 25.84%, 20.20%, 24.90%, and 14.38% belong to low, moderate, high, and very high susceptibility classes, respectively. The susceptibility map obtained from this study serves as a realistic decision-support tool for reducing landslide risk, designing infrastructure, and promoting sustainable land management in sensitive mountainous areas. Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) curve analysis was performed to measure the model's predictive performance, using the Area Under the Curve (AUC) as an overall measure of model discrimination. The ROC–AUC analysis showed an AUC value of 0.722 (72.2%), indicating acceptable model performance.

items.title: Green AI? A Critique of Green Techno-Optimism
items.abstract: This article interrogates one of the latest manifestations of the ideology of “green techno-optimism”: the belief that new digital technologies—now artificial intelligence (AI)—can and will save the planet. Drawing on political economy and energy humanities, we probe the new discourse of “green AI” which is emerging across corporate, governmental, and media spheres. While this discourse represents AI platforms and apps as capable of addressing the problem of global climate change, it also obscures their material, labor, and ecological costs. We thus critique the green techno-optimist ideology surrounding AI today in support of a greater “green tech consciousness” and “green tech conscience.” We conclude the essay with “nine laws of AI-ecology,” inspired by the “Four Laws of Ecology” Barry Commoner (1979) introduced in The Closing Circle. These distill our critique of green AI into a useful heuristic for reading what AI does to the world, and what it asks us to ignore. These laws are: (1) everything is connected to everything else; (2) everything must go somewhere; (3) nature knows best; (4) there is no such thing as a free lunch; (5) there is no infinite energy on a planet of finite resources; (6) efficiency increases consumption; (7) planned obsolescence negates efficiency gains; (8) efficiency cannot mitigate the environmental consequences of economic growth; and (9) all “green” is greenwashing. The most important task is not to make machines more intelligent in the hope that they will do the labor required to save the planet for us, but to make humans more intelligent about the true planetary consequences of AI systems, so they may find more environmentally responsible and sustainable ways of making and using AI.

items.title: Grounding Political Discourse in the Body: A Computational Approach to Analyzing U.S. Energy Narratives
items.abstract: Abstract Image schemas, recurring pre-conceptual gestalts arising from sensorimotor experience, constitute the foundational level of embodied conceptual architecture, yet their systematic identification in naturalistic language data remains a persistent methodological challenge. Traditional introspective analyses in cognitive linguistics yield rich theoretical insights but face difficulties in scalability, inter-coder reliability, and systematic replication. This study addresses these challenges by developing a computationally assisted analytical framework that integrates semantic role labeling (AllenNLP) with large language model verification (DeepSeek R1) to detect image-schematic activations in discourse. Grounded in Fairclough’s three-dimensional critical discourse analysis model, the pipeline extracts narrative triples (“agent–action–patient”) from 10 U.S. energy policy documents (74,426 characters, 289 sentences), clusters them into conceptual domains via SentenceBERT embeddings and DBSCAN, and subjects the outputs to human–LLM collaborative validation. Against a manually annotated gold standard (50 triples from 29 sentences), the pipeline achieves an F1 score of 0.79, a 20-percentage-point improvement over the raw SRL baseline. Three image schemas (CONTAINER, PATH–GOAL, and FORCE) are identified as systematically activated through specific discourse strategies. By providing structured SRL output as input to the LLM rather than requesting annotation from scratch, the pipeline reduces hallucination while preserving the directional semantic relations needed for schematic analysis. This study offers a replicable, scalable methodology for investigating embodied language in naturally occurring discourse.

items.title: HERMES–AEGIS: AI-assisted security for operational technology with structural separation from the plant
items.abstract: HERMES–AEGIS is a research programme on AI assistance for security teams in industrial plants and other critical infrastructure. It rests on three principles. First, separation by structure: no component that reads AI output is given credentials or a network path to controllers or safety systems, with the plant boundary enforced one way. Second, evidence before conclusions: every claim is tied to its source data and checked before an analyst sees it. Third, intelligence by need: each step uses the least costly sufficient AI model and escalates only when the evidence calls for it. This note sets out the problem, the principles and the current status. HERMES, the reasoning layer, exists as a research prototype exercised with simulated models; AEGIS, a read-only incident-triage application for OT security teams, is in preparation. The note includes one observational result from 7,366 public AI-agent task recordings. It is not a product announcement, makes no claim of validation against real incidents, and makes no claim of compliance with ISA/IEC 62443, NIST guidance or any regulation.

items.title: How does the visual complexity of architectural signage affect wayfinding search efficiency? Nonlinear evidence from a semantic-computational dual-channel experiment
items.abstract: Abstract Signage is the primary visual interface guiding people through complex public buildings; however, designers lack quantitative evidence on how its visual complexity shapes wayfinding performance, and clutter research largely assumes that simpler methods are always faster. This study examines whether this relationship is linear or nonmonotonic, developing the Architectural Visual Search Toolkit (AVST), a semantic-computational dual-channel framework that integrates multimodal large language model scoring with computational visual analysis to yield decomposable complexity metrics. Using AVST, 242 AI-generated signage stimuli were evaluated, and an online click-search experiment with 150 participants yielded 10,233 valid reaction-time trials analyzed via linear mixed models, analysis of variance, and bootstrap mediation. The results reveal a U-shaped relationship: medium-complexity signage produced the fastest search, whereas both low-complexity and high-complexity signage slowed it, challenging the prevailing linear assumption. Specifically, (1) color organization entropy predicted faster search; (2) mounting type moderated the complexity‒efficiency relationship; and (3) the figure‒ground index partially mediated the complexity‒reaction time pathway. These findings establish moderate complexity as an evidence-based target for wayfinding design, signage standards, and architectural planning policy.

items.title: Hubungan antara Penggunaan AI dalam Pembelajaran dan Motivasi Belajar Mahasiswa Pendidikan Guru Sekolah Dasar
items.abstract: The expanding use of artificial intelligence (AI) in learning has the potential to support students’ learning processes, but its relationship with learning motivation among Pendidikan Guru Sekolah Dasar (PGSD) students still requires investigation. This study aims to analyze the relationship between AI use in learning and learning motivation among PGSD students. The study employed a quantitative approach with a correlational design involving 38 PGSD students. Data were collected through questionnaires and analyzed using Pearson’s product–moment correlation test with SPSS. The results showed a positive and significant relationship between AI use in learning and learning motivation among PGSD students, with a relatively weak correlation (r = 0.352; p = 0.030). Students with higher levels of AI use tended to have higher learning motivation, but this relationship did not indicate causality. This study concludes that AI use in learning is associated with learning motivation among PGSD students. These findings add empirical evidence to research on AI use and learning motivation and can serve as a reference for students and educators in using AI wisely and responsibly as a learning aid. Future research should involve more respondents and examine other factors associated with students’ learning motivation.

items.title: Human-AI Interaction in the Metaverse: A Maqasid al-Shariah Conceptual Framework for Autonomous Agents, Virtual Governance, and Moral Education
items.abstract: The rapid convergence of artificial intelligence and immersive virtual environments has given rise to the Metaverse, a persistent digital space in which autonomous AI agents increasingly mediate human social, economic, and educational interaction. Existing Islamic legal scholarship has examined the legal capacity of AI and has proposed maqasid-based governance for Islamic finance and for national regulation, but it has not yet shown how the legal status of autonomous agents, governance in a space without a single jurisdiction, and moral education in immersive settings depend on one another. This study addresses that gap by asking how maqasid al-Shariah and the classical doctrine of legal capacity (al-ahliyyah) can ground a conceptual framework for autonomous agents, virtual governance, and moral education in the Metaverse. Using a qualitative library research method, the study analyzes classical fiqh concepts alongside contemporary Islamic legal scholarship on artificial intelligence, robotics, and digital ethics, and situates them within the secular literature on metaverse governance and virtual moral education. The study advances three conceptual propositions. First, autonomous AI agents cannot bear full legal or moral responsibility (taklif) because they lack the volition and consciousness required by Islamic legal theory, yet a bounded, functional capacity can be recognized for practical governance purposes, with liability ultimately resting with human developers, operators, and institutions. Second, the five maqasid can be mapped onto the governance gaps documented in secular metaverse scholarship to yield a jurisdiction-independent review checklist. Third, immersive moral education is compatible with tarbiyah only when its design is governed by explicit safeguards. The main contribution of this study is an integrated, maqasid-based framework that links these three areas, which have so far been examined separately. The findings are conceptual and normative rather than empirically tested, and they carry practical implications for Islamic financial and educational institutions designing metaverse platforms and AI agents intended for Muslim users.

items.title: Human-Centred Change Management for AI Adoption in Government: Adapting ADKAR for the Algorithmic State
items.abstract: Governments are introducing artificial intelligence (AI) into grievance handling, welfare targeting, health, revenue administration and many other functions. Experience with earlier e-government programmes shows that the human side of such change — whether officers understand, trust and use new tools appropriately — decides success as much as the technology. AI adds new challenges to familiar change-management problems: outputs are probabilistic rather than deterministic, the reasoning can be opaque, roles and discretion shift, and both over-reliance and under-use are risks. This paper adapts the widely used ADKAR model (Awareness, Desire, Knowledge, Ability, Reinforcement) to AI adoption in public administration. For each stage it identifies AI-specific barriers, practical interventions and indicators. It adds a sixth element — Accountability — to address the distinctive governance requirement that a human officer remains answerable for decisions supported by AI. The resulting "ADKAR+A" model is offered as a practical planning tool for programme leaders, illustrated with examples from Indian state e-governance contexts, and complemented by a ten-point readiness checklist. The paper draws on the author's experience in large public-sector digital transformation programmes and on published research; it is a conceptual contribution and does not report an evaluation.

items.title: Identification and Validation of Components Affecting the Sustainability of the National Banking Network
items.abstract: The present study was conducted with the aim of identifying and validating the components affecting the sustainability of the banking network, using both qualitative and quantitative phases. In the qualitative phase, a meta-synthesis approach was employed, and based on a systematic search of reputable scientific databases, 79 articles were identified. After applying the inclusion and exclusion criteria, 16 selected studies were analyzed. The findings of this phase indicated that in the economic and financial dimension, components such as operational efficiency and sustainable profitability, credit and liquidity risk management, capital adequacy and balance sheet structure, exposure to foreign exchange risk, and asset quality play a significant role in banking stability. In the institutional and corporate governance dimension, ownership structure, effective supervisory systems, and macroeconomic conditions were identified as key factors. In the technological dimension, components such as digital transformation, development of modern banking infrastructure, cybersecurity, and the use of artificial intelligence for risk management were found to be of particular importance. In the social dimension, banks’ social responsibility, transparency in communications, and enhancement of customer experience were identified as influential factors affecting public trust and social capital. In the quantitative phase, confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) was employed to validate the components extracted from the qualitative analysis. The results indicate that the sustainability of the banking network requires an integrated approach that simultaneously strengthens the economic, institutional, technological, and social dimensions.

items.title: Identifying Key Factors and Drivers Affecting Sustainable Auditing Based on Sustainability Reporting
items.abstract: The present study aimed to identify the key factors and strategic drivers affecting sustainable auditing within the framework of sustainability reporting. This applied research was conducted using a descriptive-survey methodology with a futures studies approach. The study employed a paradigmatic qualitative model as the foundation for hypothesis development and cause-and-effect analysis. Data were collected using a researcher-made questionnaire distributed through block random sampling among experts and specialists in auditing, accounting, and futures studies. The cross-impact analysis method (MICMAC) was applied to analyze the relationships among variables and identify influential and dependent components. An 8×8 matrix was completed by six experts who evaluated the degree of influence among variables using a four-point scale ranging from no impact to strong impact. The research process also incorporated Delphi rounds and scenario analysis to identify possible future states of sustainable auditing. The findings demonstrated that uncertainty, social trust, and auditor independence were classified as linkage and risk variables with high influence and dependence, while technology emerged as the strongest influential variable in the system. Stakeholder pressure was identified as an autonomous variable, whereas institutional challenge, auditor role, and sustainability linkage were classified as dependent variables. MICMAC analysis revealed a matrix fill rate of 87.5%, indicating a highly interconnected system among the identified components. Strategic variables affecting the future of sustainable auditing included technology, uncertainty, social trust, and auditor independence. Furthermore, four future scenarios were extracted: symbolic auditing, trust-regulating institution, reactive-minimal auditing, and predictive and strategic auditing. The results indicated that the future evolution of sustainable auditing depends significantly on technological advancement, regulatory maturity, professional competencies, stakeholder pressure, and the intelligent use of artificial intelligence and ESG-based analytical systems. The study concluded that sustainable auditing is evolving from a traditional compliance-oriented activity toward a future-oriented institutional mechanism for trust creation and strategic governance. The integration of technology, sustainability legitimacy, auditor independence, and uncertainty management plays a critical role in shaping the effectiveness of sustainable auditing systems. The proposed framework provides a comprehensive basis for policymakers, regulators, and professional auditing bodies to improve sustainability assurance practices and strengthen organizational accountability in response to environmental, social, and governance challenges.

items.title: Impact of Artificial Intelligence in Finance and Decision Making
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence is increasingly used in financial services for fraud detection, credit assessment, investment support and digital banking, yet its adoption depends on how users perceive its benefits, risks and trustworthiness. This study examines user perceptions of artificial intelligence in finance, focusing on perceived benefits, perceived risks, trust, explainability, perceived usefulness, adoption intention and perceived effectiveness of financial decisions. A quantitative, cross-sectional design was used, and primary data were collected from 30 respondents through a structured online questionnaire. Descriptive statistics, Cronbach alpha reliability analysis and Spearman rank correlation with Holm adjustment for multiple testing were applied. Perceived benefits and perceived usefulness were positively associated with adoption intention, and adoption intention was positively associated with perceived decision effectiveness; all three associations remained significant after adjustment. The expected negative association between perceived risk and adoption intention was not found, and the trust and explainability hypotheses were not supported. Because the sample was small and concentrated among young respondents in information technology occupations, the findings are exploratory and should not be generalized. The results suggest that perceived value is linked with willingness to use artificial intelligence based financial tools, while the roles of trust and risk need further study.

items.title: Implications of Age and Parity on Squamocolumnar Junction (SCJ) Visibility for Implementing Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Cervical Cancer Screening: Multi-Country Evidence From the PAVE Study
items.abstract: PURPOSE Extended HPV-based screening and automated visual evaluation (AVE) may improve cervical cancer screening in resource-limited settings (RLS), but these tools should work well across different groups of women. The HPV–Automated Visual Evaluation (PAVE) approach is promising. Regardless, its performance may be limited by whether the SCJ (a marker of the transformation zone) can be seen on the cervix. We examined how age and parity affect SCJ visibility and how SCJ visibility influences AVE performance, with a focus on implementation challenges in RLS. METHODS We analyzed 5,754 cervical images from HPV-positive women in the nine-country PAVE study (Brazil, Cambodia, Dominican Republic, El Salvador, Eswatini, Honduras, Malawi, Nigeria, Tanzania). PAVE scientific experts independently classified blinded participant characteristics images taken after acetic acid application as SCJ “not visible,” “partially visible,” and “fully visible.” We assessed associations between SCJ visibility, patient characteristics (age, parity), and AVE's performance in predicting high-grade cervical lesions (CIN3+). RESULTS SCJ visibility declined with age. The proportion of women with a non-visible SCJ increased from 7.2% among women aged 25-29 to 21.3% among women aged 45-49. Full SCJ visibility decreased with age. Parity also mattered. Non-visible SCJ was more common among women who had never given vaginal birth (increased from 11.4% in women who had ≥5 children to 22.4% in nulliparous women); this increased further at older ages. Considered together, the effect became stronger; 42.3% of nulliparous women aged 45-49 had a non-visible SCJ, compared with 15.0% of parous women. AVE performance was better when the SCJ was visible (OR 4.3), associating severe visual classification and case status, and weaker when it was not visible (OR 2.4). Older and nulliparous women are more likely to have non-visible SCJ, limiting AI-assisted visual triage performance in RLS. HPV positivity without visible lesions in these populations poses a critical management challenge. To achieve equitable global cervical cancer control as AI-enabled cervical screening expands globally, settings lacking robust surveillance should develop tailored management strategies for these specific subgroups.

items.title: IN SILICO INVESTIGATION FOR MODELING ISATIN DERIVATIVES AS ANTI-COLORECTAL CANCER AGENTS ASSISTED BY MOLECULAR DOCKING
items.abstract: The present paper introduces an in silico study using quantitative structure-activity relationship (QSAR) for the possibility of developing anti-colorectal cancer from isatin derivatives. The theoretical treatments were carried out using quantum mechanical calculations for 29 compounds, with 25 as the training set and the rest as the test set. The results indicate that the estimated properties as descriptors are not adequate for building the QSAR model. It was found that the outcome parameters from the docking study are quite effective to be used as descriptors in building the model. Two QSAR models were developed for estimating the cytotoxic activity data IC50 regarding the colon cancer (HCT-116) cell line utilizing the binding energy that resulted from the docking study as a descriptor. It wasconcluded that the significance of this research extends beyond the prediction of new compounds and the reduction of trial-and-error approaches in chemistry through introducing the resulting binding energy from the docking study as a descriptor. In the long term, these computational strategies may be integrated with artificial intelligence to suggest the most suitable compounds for specific diseases. Such advancement could represent a qualitative leap in drug discovery by reducing economic costs, minimizing environmental impact, decreasing human effort, and significantly shortening the required development time.

items.title: IN SILICO TOXICITY SCREENING: FROM CONVENTIONAL TO DIGITAL TOXICOLOGY
items.abstract: Toxicity remains a major consideration in drug discovery because a compound must combine therapeutic activity with an acceptable safety profile. Conventional toxicity testing provides essential biological evidence but can be resource-intensive and may be difficult to apply to large chemical libraries at an early stage. In silico toxicity screening provides a complementary, data-driven approach for identifying potential safety liabilities before extensive experimental testing. This review summarises the transition from conventional toxicology to digital toxicology and discusses quantitative structure–activity relationship (QSAR) modelling, read-across, molecular docking, toxicokinetic modelling, machine learning, deep learning and artificial intelligence (AI) approaches. Major toxicity endpoints, including cardiotoxicity, hepatotoxicity, nephrotoxicity, neurotoxicity, genotoxicity, carcinogenicity, reproductive and developmental toxicity, immunotoxicity and respiratory toxicity, are considered from a computational perspective. The article also examines how computational methods can support ADMET profiling, lead optimisation, candidate prioritisation and early toxicity-based deprioritisation. Although digital methods can improve speed, scalability and consistency, their reliability depends on data quality, model validation, applicability domain, interpretability and experimental confirmation. Future toxicology is expected to increasingly integrate AI, multi-omics, human-relevant in vitro systems, organ-on-chip models and New Approach Methodologies (NAMs). Overall, computational toxicity assessment is best viewed as a complementary component of an integrated safety strategy rather than a replacement for experimental toxicology.

items.title: INJECTABLE NANOROBOTS: EMERGING FRONTIERS IN PRECISION DRUG DELIVERY, DISEASE, DIAGNOSIS, AND TARGETED THERAPEUTICS –A COMPREHENSIVE REVIEW
items.abstract: The most exciting development in nanomedicine is the injectable nanorobots that combine nanotechnology, robotics, biotechnology, materials science, and artificial intelligence for extremely accurate illness detection and treatment. In contrast to conventional drug delivery systems that disperse medication throughout the body, injectable nanorobots are engineered to navigate bodily fluids, detect disease-specific biomarkers, and release therapeutic agents selectively at the target site. These systems have demonstrated significant potential in areas such as cancer, cardiovascular disease, neurological conditions, infectious diseases, regenerative medicine, and precision diagnostics. Recent advancements in enzyme-powered, magnetic, ultrasound-driven, and biohybrid nanorobots have expedited the transfer of these technologies from lab research to preclinical and early translational investigations. Biocompatibility, biodegradability, large-scale production, real-time navigation, regulatory approval, and long-term biosafety are some of the issues that still need to be resolved despite the tremendous advancements. The present understanding of injectable nanorobots, including their historical evolution, classification, structural elements, fabrication techniques, propulsion mechanisms, targeting tactics, biological applications, safety issues, and potential future clinical uses, is compiled in this review. A thorough overview of this quickly developing topic discusses recent developments and new trends.

items.title: Instructor Authority and Generative AI in Japanese Writing Instruction
items.abstract: The spread of generative artificial intelligence in higher education has begun to change writing classrooms in ways that are not always immediately visible. In second language education, students now revise and refine texts through AI-supported interaction before teachers ever see the final product. This shift raises questions not only about writing quality, but also about how teachers understand, evaluate, and guide the writing process itself. In Japanese writing instruction, where revision often depends on close attention to context, nuance, and interpersonal positioning, these changes carry particular weight. This study examines how ten instructors of Japanese writing at Hanoi University perceive the growing presence of generative AI in their teaching. Based on survey data and qualitative interpretation, the analysis shows that writing instruction remains deeply dependent on teacher labor, especially in areas that require contextual judgment and individualized feedback. At the same time, many instructors described a growing sense of uncertainty. When revision happens through AI outside the classroom, it becomes harder to determine what a student can actually do alone, and this weakens confidence in conventional forms of assessment. Some participants also felt that the teacher’s traditional role as the central source of correction is becoming less stable. Yet this did not lead them to view AI as a replacement. Instead, they emphasized that meaning-making in Japanese writing still relies on human sensitivity to social context and rhetorical intention. Rather than simply introducing efficiency, generative AI appears to be changing the balance of authority in writing education itself.

items.title: Integrating Artificial Intelligence and Islamic Commercial Law to Enable Online Transactions Free of Gharar
items.abstract: The advancement of digital technology has brought significant changes to economic transaction systems, shfting from conventional face to face transactions to online based transactions. This transformation offers greater convenience and efficiency homever, it also raises various legal issues, practicularly concerning transparency, fairness, and te clarity of information in transactions. From the perspective of Islamic commercial law, this situation has the potential to give rise to elements of gharar due to limitations in direct verification and information asymmetry. This study aims to analyze the integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in minimizing gharar in digital transactions. The method used is a qualitative approach with a normative-empirical research design through literature review and interviews with practitioners and academics. The analysis is conducted descriptively-analytically and comparatively between AI practices and Sharia principles. The results indicate that AI plays a role in enhancing transparency through data verification, fraud detection, and real-time information presentation, thereby supporting the principles of bayan, taradi, and hifz al-mal. However, the potential for gharar may still arise if algorithms lack transparency, are biased, or are misused. Therefore, human oversight and Sharia audits are necessary to ensure that the use of AI remains in line with the principles of justice and public interest in Islamic economic transactions.

items.title: Integration of Static Knowledge and Telemetry Data for an IoT-Based Customer Support AI Agent
items.abstract: The operational effectiveness of artificial intelligence agents in customer support is frequently attributed to the generative sophistication of underlying language models, although answer reliability primarily depends on the structure and quality of the referenced knowledge base. In complex technical domains such as the Internet of Things (IoT), static documentation alone often fails to resolve customer inquiries that involve real-time device states, sensor readings, and connectivity logs. This study investigates how progressive tiers of knowledge integration affect the response quality of an AI agent within an IoT customer support context. Employing a mixed-method pilot design combining literature synthesis, comparative analysis, experimental testing, and conceptual exploration, thirty representative questions were classified into informational, status, and diagnostic categories. These queries were evaluated across four operational scenarios: without retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), article-based RAG, article plus device metadata records, and a comprehensive hybrid framework integrating static articles, device records, and telemetry streams. Answer quality was measured using Cosine Similarity, BERTScore (F1), and a randomized blind human evaluation assessing relevance, correctness, and usefulness. The results demonstrate that while curated static documentation adequately addresses procedural informational queries, resolving status and diagnostic issues necessitates real-time operational context. The hybrid integration delivered the highest overall performance, achieving a human-evaluation score of 4.40 compared with 2.53 for article-based RAG (p = 0.0039). These empirical findings confirm that robust IoT support agents require dynamic knowledge governance that bridges versioned documentation, synchronized asset metadata, and live telemetry data within a unified retrieval framework.

items.title: Integrative Digital Governance for Deepfake Harms: Bridging Legal Regulation, Public Policy, and Victim Protection in Indonesia
items.abstract: Deepfake related harms expose a governance problem that cannot be resolved through criminalisation alone. Synthetic images, audio, and video can generate reputational, sexual, economic, privacy, and identity harms while circulating through infrastructures operated by multiple private and public actors. This study examines how Indonesia’s existing legal and public policy architecture addresses deepfake harms and develops an integrative digital governance model oriented toward prevention and victim protection. The research uses normative legal analysis with statutory, conceptual, policy, and limited comparative approaches. Primary materials include Indonesia’s Electronic Information and Transactions Law, Personal Data Protection Law, Criminal Code, Sexual Violence Crime Law, electronic system regulations, and national artificial intelligence policy instruments. Comparative lessons are drawn from the European Union’s AI transparency regime, Australia’s online safety model, and South Korea’s response to synthetic sexual abuse. The analysis finds that Indonesia possesses several applicable legal instruments, but they operate through separate legal interests, institutions, and remedial logics. This fragmentation leaves four governance deficits: weak ex ante authenticity safeguards, unclear platform due diligence standards, dispersed enforcement coordination, and victim remedies that are insufficiently rapid for viral synthetic content. The article proposes an Integrative Digital Governance framework consisting of prevention and authenticity, platform accountability, coordinated enforcement, and victim recovery. Its contribution lies in shifting Indonesian deepfake scholarship from offence by offence legal mapping toward a lifecycle-based governance architecture that connects regulation, institutional responsibility, technological safeguards, and measurable victim-centred outcomes.

items.abstract: The incorporation of artificial intelligence into accounting activities has generated new possibilities for process automation, information processing, and professional decision-making support. This study aimed to analyze the perception and use of artificial intelligence tools in accounting decision-making among professionals in Guayaquil. A quantitative, non-experimental, cross-sectional study was conducted through a survey administered to professionals working in accounting-related areas. From a population of 307 accountants approached, 222 valid responses were obtained through non-probability convenience sampling. The findings showed that 67.57% of participants considered that artificial intelligence tools improve the accuracy of accounting decisions, while 61.26% reported using them for this type of decision-making. Likewise, 76.58% indicated that these tools reduce the time required to make decisions. A statistically significant association was identified between age and willingness to use artificial intelligence, χ²(3) = 68.63, p < .001, with a Cramer's V of .56. The findings suggest that artificial intelligence has a favorable perception among the professionals studied, although its implementation requires training, human oversight, and ethical criteria.

items.title: Intelligent Cyber Defense Technology for Urban Rail Transit Systems: Conceptual Foundations and Future Prospects
items.abstract: SignificanceIn recent years, the rapid advancement of industrial digitalization and intelligentization has extended the boundaries of cyberspace into the physical world, and urban rail transit systems, as critical national information infrastructure, have been exposed to increasingly severe cybersecurity threats. The network environment of urban rail industrial control systems is characterized by wide-area deployment, dynamic evolution, and strong heterogeneity. Extensive network coverage, dynamically changing operating conditions, and diverse equipment types and communication protocols impose higher requirements on the timeliness, accuracy, adaptability, and coordination capabilities of cybersecurity defenses. Conventional cybersecurity defenses often lack sufficient awareness and remain reactive in these environments, making timely and accurate discovery and identification of wide-area network threats difficult. Static and passive protection mechanisms cannot be readily adjusted to changes in network conditions and threats, while unified management and coordination of heterogeneous cybersecurity devices remain insufficient. Consequently, limited accuracy and timeliness in threat monitoring, static and passive defense mechanisms, and weak unified management and coordination capabilities remain major technical challenges. These challenges are further complicated by the interconnection of control centers, stations, train networks, and cloud platforms, through which threats may be propagated across different operational domains. Meanwhile, strict requirements for train operation safety, real-time control, and service continuity must be satisfied during security monitoring and defensive operations. Timely threat discovery must therefore be reconciled with accurate identification, and defensive policies must be adapted to changing network conditions and threat patterns. Research on artificial immunity and large language models is consequently needed to support the recognition of unfamiliar threats, the dynamic optimization of defensive policies, and the coordinated management of heterogeneous cybersecurity devices.ProgressTo address these challenges, artificial immunity and large language models were incorporated into a research framework for complex urban rail industrial control networks. Timely and accurate wide-area threat discovery, proactive defense against dynamically evolving threats, and collaborative orchestration of heterogeneous cybersecurity devices were identified as the three principal research problems. Three core techniques together with an integrated prototype system were included in the proposed framework. Specifically, an artificial-immune-recognition-based risk monitoring method was proposed to enable rapid threat detection and precise identification. Multisource heterogeneous data were considered for feature fusion and representation in a unified immune feature space. Traffic, logs, alerts, protocol commands, and equipment states were included among the information sources. Hierarchical clustering and detector tolerance training were incorporated into the detector generation scheme, and rapid responses within detector clusters were proposed to improve monitoring efficiency. A dual-verification mechanism was introduced, in which preliminary screening with self detectors was followed by further identification with non-self detectors. An artificial-immune-evolution-based proactive defense framework was then proposed to enhance protection against persistent and multistage attacks. Clonal proliferation and hierarchical differential evolution were incorporated into threat gene evolution to support the exploration of potential threat patterns. Stochastic attack-defense games and deep learning were combined in the proposed technical route for defense policy generation and adaptive dynamic optimization. Successive states, available actions, immediate rewards and costs, and expected future returns were considered in the game-based modeling of attack-defense interactions. A large-language-model-based collaborative management approach was also presented to coordinate diverse security devices for joint defense. Heterogeneous threat intelligence was organized within a cloud-edge-endpoint architecture for collection, aggregation, compression, and storage. The knowledge reasoning and generation capabilities of large language models were incorporated into intelligence analysis and the generation of cross-domain coordination plans. Risk monitoring systems, proactive defense systems, firewalls, and cryptographic appliances were included among the intended managed devices. Policy consistency checks, coordinated distribution, execution verification, and audit records were incorporated into the system design. Building upon this foundation, a prototype intelligent cybersecurity defense architecture was presented for urban rail transit systems, and system integration, deployment arrangements, and technical validation were outlined.Conclusions and ProspectsAn integrated research framework was proposed for cybersecurity defense in urban rail transit systems, with risk monitoring, proactive defense, and coordinated device management connected through three complementary technical directions. Artificial immune recognition was introduced for timely threat discovery and accurate identification, immune evolution was incorporated into adaptive defense policy generation, and large language models were introduced for heterogeneous threat intelligence analysis and collaborative device management. A technical route beyond traditional patch-based passive defense was thereby outlined to support the secure and reliable operation of national critical information infrastructure. Further research should be directed toward the adaptation of these techniques to actual urban rail operating conditions. Dynamic self-boundary modeling and unknown-threat recognition should be refined in response to changes in operating schedules, equipment conditions, and maintenance activities. Defense policy generation and optimization should be investigated under the constraints of train operation safety, real-time control, and service continuity. The explainability and traceability of generated management plans, cross-device policy consistency, and coordinated execution should also be strengthened. items.title: Investigation and Analysis of the Age-Friendly Dilemma of Smart Elderly Care Services under AI Empowerment
items.abstract: Against the backdrop of population aging and the widespread adoption of digital technologies, artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being integrated into home- and community-based eldercare. However, many older adults continue to face a digital divide, while smart eldercare products often provide only superficial age-friendly adaptations and fail to match users' needs. This study examines older residents of urban communities and their family members. Drawing on a literature review, a questionnaire survey, and semi-structured interviews, it investigates the development of AI-enabled smart eldercare services and the difficulties older adults encounter when using smart devices and related services. Informed by digital divide theory, active aging theory, and supply-and-demand matching theory, the study analyzes the factors underlying these difficulties and proposes a smart eldercare service model that uses age-friendly short videos as a delivery medium and intergenerational collaboration as its core mechanism. It further develops operational strategies across six dimensions: content, target groups, channels, technology, implementation, and operations. Survey findings are used to assess the model's feasibility. The proposed approach offers communities and social organizations a low-cost, practical framework for more inclusive smart eldercare services, with the aim of narrowing the digital divide and supporting active aging.

items.title: ISLAMIC ETHICS AND THE CRISIS OF DIGITAL INTEGRITY: A CRITICAL ANALYSIS OF TRUTH, DECEPTION AND RESPONSIBILITY IN THE AGE OF GENERATIVE AI
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) can now produce fluent text, realistic images and convincing audio at almost no cost, and it does so without any commitment to truth. This has created a crisis of digital integrity: fabricated content is hard to distinguish from authentic content, machine outputs present invented claims as fact, and it is unclear who should answer for the resulting harm. Mainstream AI ethics has responded with principles such as transparency and accountability, but these frameworks draw mainly on Western philosophical traditions and treat deception largely as a technical or regulatory problem. Islamic scholarship on AI has grown quickly, yet most of it addresses AI in general through maqasid al-shariah, and its treatment of misinformation relies almost entirely on the receiver's duty of tabayyun (verification). This concept paper critically analyses truth, deception and responsibility in generative AI through Islamic ethics. Using conceptual analysis and theory adaptation, it synthesises the empirical literature on synthetic media with Qur'anic, prophetic and juristic concepts. It argues that Islamic ethics offers an integrated account built on three pillars: sidq (truthfulness) as a duty owed by every speaker and publisher, the prohibition of ghish, tadlis and kadhib (deception, concealment and falsehood) as limits on design and deployment, and amanah and mas'uliyyah (trust and answerability) as a model of responsibility that always returns to a human agent. The paper proposes a Digital Integrity Framework that distributes these duties across developers, deployers, users and regulators, and offers suggestions for policy, education and future research.

items.title: Judgment in AI Policy Advice: Humans-in-the-Loop, Appreciation, and the DOGE Experience
items.abstract: Recent studies of Policy Advisory Systems (PAS) focus on the quality of advice and how it is designed and managed. This article extends this analysis looking at the impact of Artificial Intelligence (AI) on advisory systems’ behaviour and activity using Geoffrey Vickers’ concept of policy judgment. It notes how negligible user costs combined with the apparent robustness of AI computational outputs can generate advice that can exercise an important and independent influence on policy decisions and outcomes, despite that advice not always being accurate or well-considered. In this sense AI-generated advice shares some of the same characteristics of earlier mechanical algorithms framing policy problems and recommendations for action which lack the hallmarks of careful appreciation of the issues at stake. This is illustrated by the use of AI tools by the US Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE) in 2025-2026, in particular its directive to autonomously reduce the number and size of contracts and grants made by many Departments, and specifically the US Department of Veterans Affairs. The case underlines that a crucial design challenge for AI-based policy advice is to go beyond only trying to ensure human oversight or a ‘Human-in-the-Loop’ in order to ensure that problems are properly articulated and actions towards them are sound.

items.title: Kemampuan Berpikir Kritis Generasi Z di Era Artificial Intelligence dan Media Sosial: Perspektif Teori Paulo Freire
items.abstract: The presence of artificial intelligence (AI) and social media has transformed Generation Z’s patterns of learning, information seeking, and everyday interaction. However, previous research findings have not yielded consistent conclusions regarding the effects of these two technologies on critical thinking skills, while studies interpreting them through Paulo Freire’s critical education perspective remain limited. This study aims to analyze the partial and simultaneous effects of AI use and social media use intensity on Generation Z’s critical thinking skills and to interpret the results from Paulo Freire’s perspective. The study employed a quantitative approach with an explanatory survey design involving 100 Generation Z respondents selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected using an online questionnaire and analyzed through multiple linear regression with the assistance of SPSS. The findings indicate that AI use had no significant partial effect on critical thinking skills (p = 0.416), nor did the intensity of social media use (p = 0.198). Simultaneously, the two variables also had no significant effect on critical thinking skills (p = 0.435) and explained only 1.7% of the variation in these skills (R² = 0.017). These findings are consistent with Paulo Freire’s thought, which positions dialogue, reflection, and praxis as the primary elements in developing critical thinking skills rather than technology alone. This study concludes that AI and social media are not direct determinants of critical thinking skills but rather learning tools whose benefits depend on how users utilize, evaluate, and reflect on information. Theoretically, this study enriches educational research in the digital era by integrating Freire’s critical education perspective. Practically, these findings emphasize the importance of reflective learning, information verification, and dialogical methods in developing Generation Z’s critical thinking skills.

items.title: Leadership Practices and Employee Motivation of Selected Tenant General Contractors in a Medium-Scale Commercial Project: Basis for a Workforce Engagement Program
items.abstract: This study examined the relationship between leadership practices and employee motivation among construction workers employed by selected tenant general contractors in a medium-scale commercial project in Santa Rosa, Laguna, Philippines, as a basis for developing a Workforce Engagement Program. Anchored in Full-Range Leadership Theory and Self-Determination Theory, the study employed a quantitative descriptive-correlational research design involving 63 construction workers from five tenant general contractors selected through total enumeration. Data were collected using an expert-validated structured survey questionnaire and analyzed using frequency, percentage, weighted mean, and Pearson product-moment correlation. Findings revealed that most respondents had limited construction experience and relatively short company tenure. Leadership practices were generally perceived positively, with supervisory support receiving the highest weighted mean (3.76), while recognition and appreciation received the lowest (2.82), indicating weaknesses in formal monetary and non-monetary recognition. Employee motivation was generally high, particularly intrinsic motivation (3.72), followed by professional growth (3.58) and extrinsic motivation (3.57). However, the relationship between leadership practices and employee motivation was statistically nonsignificant (r = −0.022, p = 0.864). The study proposed KILOS-KAPWA: A Construction Workforce Engagement and Recognition Program to strengthen supervisory communication, employee recognition, professional development, workplace support, and participatory decision-making. The findings align with Sustainable Development Goal 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth) and Sustainable Development Goal 9 (Industry, Innovation and Infrastructure). The proposed program may contribute to organizational and socioeconomic sustainability by supporting workforce engagement, employee development, and responsible construction workforce management, although its effectiveness requires evaluation following implementation.

items.abstract: Deploying generative artificial intelligence and deep computer vision architectures into production environments requires overcoming strict hardware memory ceilings, cloud API rate throttling, structural output hallucinations, and real-time latency bounds. This paper presents a unified empirical study of three production-grade artificial intelligence systems engineered specifically for resource-constrained execution across local workstations, cloud-hybrid inference pipelines, and edge vision monitors: (1) A privacy-first, local multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) architecture utilizing 384-dimensional sentence transformers dense embeddings indexed inside an embedded sqlite-vec engine, a dual-layer visual inference router failing over automatically from cloud Qwen 27B (via the Featherless API) to a locally hosted Moondream vision-language model, and a memory-bounded local phi3 inference engine via Ollama constrained to a strict 4,096-token context ceiling to guarantee a 0% out-of-memory (OOM) crash rate; (2) An end-to-end Large Language Model (LLM) evaluation, post-training alignment via Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) and Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF), and feedback intelligence framework benchmarking Aspect-Based, Few-Shot, and Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting strategies to achieve 99.5% classification accuracy and a 90% reduction in end-to-end processing latency, sustained by a stateful Dynamic API Key Rotation middleware that bypasses the 15 Requests-Per-Minute (15 RPM) free-tier Google Gemini API rate ceiling, alongside deterministic JSON tool-calling schema verification and multimodal reasoning fine-tuning on VEO-3 and Gemini; and (3) A real-time computer vision safety and industrial inspection suite comprising a hybrid ResNet-50 and dlib Eye Aspect Ratio (EAR) ensemble for driver microsleep detection (achieving 92% classification accuracy, 35% fewer false positive alerts, and strictly < 100 ms per-frame inference latency across 10,000+ video frames) paired with an OpenCV and TensorFlow-Keras Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) predictive maintenance pipeline for micro-tool wear classification across 5,000+ augmented images (expanded 100× from 50+ base microscopy images) and 100+ milling intervals using 3 extracted morphological wear descriptors (achieving 75% multi-class classification accuracy).

items.title: LONG-ACTING INJECTABLES DRUG DELIVERY LINKING RELEASE MECHANISMS, PLATFORM DESIGN AND THERAPEUTIC APPLICATIONS
items.abstract: Long-acting injectables (LAIs) are innovative drug-delivery systems allowing for prolonged controlled release of a drug after a single administration. By decreasing the dosing frequency, long-acting injectable can have a positive impact on treatment compliance, patient convenience, and drug exposure while minimising the peak–trough fluctuations. This review provides an overview of the different formulation approaches used to develop LAIs, including microspheres, Nano crystal suspensions, oil-based depots, in situ forming depots, implants, hydrogels, lyotropic liquid crystalline systems, polymer-lipid hybrids, and modified protein and peptide therapeutics. The review highlights the main advantages and limitations of LAIs, such as patient adherence and consistent drug exposure, while also discussing injection site reactions, prolonged drug exposure, challenges of flexible dose adjustment, manufacturing complexity, and cost. Storage requirements will be discussed. The clinical applications in schizophrenia and bipolar disorder, HIV treatment and prevention, opioid use disorder, growth hormone deficiency, and diabetes. Ophthalmic diseases will be highlighted together with the marketed products in each therapeutic area. Finally, emerging technologies, patient-friendly LAI approaches, biomaterials, artificial intelligence, predictive modelling, and personalised medicine are discussed. In conclusion, LAIs are an important class of drug delivery systems that can have a significant impact on optimal and sustained drug exposure while decreasing the treatment burden on the patient. The complexity of the different formulation approaches and the need for clinical development expertise are still major hurdles that industry is currently trying to address by developing new approaches and manufacturing processes.

items.title: Machine Learning and Explainable Artificial Intelligence for Predicting 10-Year Mortality after Cardiac Surgery: A Retrospective Cohort Study
items.abstract: Abstract Background Preoperative neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) is associated with short-term outcomes after cardiac surgery, but its value for long-term mortality prediction remains unclear. We developed a machine learning model incorporating NLR to predict 10-year all-cause mortality after cardiac surgery, and used explainable artificial intelligence to interpret the role of NLR. Methods We included adult patients undergoing elective cardiac surgery from the MIMIC-IV database. The primary outcome was 10-year all-cause mortality. Six machine learning models were compared using grid search, stratified 5-fold cross-validation, and bootstrap internal validation. The best model was interpreted using SHAP on the test set. The NLR cutoff was identified by piecewise regression on the training set. Calibration curves and decision curve analysis were used to evaluate model performance. Results Among 4,891 patients (median age 68 years), 222 (4.54%) died within 10 years. After tuning, XGBoost performed best (optimism-corrected AUC = 0.815; 95% CI: 0.758–0.861), outperforming LASSO regression (AUC = 0.780). NLR alone had an AUC of 0.709, similar to APACHE III (0.732; P = 0.630). Combining NLR with APACHE III improved the AUC to 0.761 (P = 0.002). SHAP analysis identified APACHE III (0.371) and NLR (0.291) as the top two predictors. Piecewise regression identified an NLR cutoff of 6.5. At a 15% risk threshold, the positive predictive value was 23.3% (5.1-fold enrichment). Decision curve analysis showed net benefit across thresholds of 5%-30%. Conclusions Preoperative NLR is an independent predictor of 10-year mortality after cardiac surgery, with performance comparable to APACHE III. The tuned XGBoost model showed good overall performance. An NLR threshold of 6.5 was identified and supported by SHAP analysis. NLR may complement existing risk scores for long-term risk stratification, but should not be used as a standalone tool.

items.abstract: Teacher human resource quality improvement management is an important aspect of efforts to improve the quality of education in schools. This study aims to analyze teacher human resource quality improvement management in improving the quality of education at SMA Negeri 1 Pamekasan. This study used a descriptive qualitative approach involving the principal, vice principal for curriculum affairs, teachers, and school documentation as data sources. Data were collected through interviews, observation, and documentation, then analyzed through the stages of data reduction, data presentation, and conclusion drawing. Data validity was confirmed through source triangulation and technique triangulation. The results show that teacher quality improvement was carried out through needs-based planning by utilizing SWOT analysis and the education report card, as well as the implementation of various development programs, such as In-House Training (IHT), MGMP, supervision, technology training, and the use of artificial intelligence (AI) in learning. Teacher quality improvement contributed to more active learning, increased student creativity and achievement, and improved school education report card results. However, its implementation still faced challenges in the form of technological adaptation and resistance to change among senior teachers. This study contributes to the development of educational human resource management studies, particularly in strengthening teacher quality as a strategic factor in improving school quality. The implications of this study emphasize the importance of teacher development planning that is needs-based, sustainable, and responsive to the transformation of learning technology.

items.title: Mapping Artificial Intelligence Research in Strategic Management: A Bibliometric Analysis and Future Research Agenda
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly embedded in strategic decision-making, competitive positioning, innovation management, organizational learning, and governance, yet the literature remains fragmented across management, information systems, innovation, and technology-management fields. This study provides a focused bibliometric review of AI research in strategic management. Scopus was used as the primary database, and the query "artificial intelligence" AND "strategic management" was applied to titles, abstracts, and keywords, with restrictions to Business, Management and Accounting, Article and Review document types, and English-language publications. From 126 retrieved records, relevance screening excluded 82 records, leaving 44 publications for analysis. The study examines annual trends, citation patterns, keyword co-occurrence, country distribution, science maps, TCCM synthesis, and a WoS/SSCI sensitivity analysis. Results show slow development before 2018 and marked acceleration after 2023, with 2026 treated as an incomplete year. Themes are shifting from decision support and strategic planning toward generative AI, innovation management, sustainability, organizational capabilities, and governance. By combining bibliometric mapping, TCCM, and cross-database sensitivity analysis, this study offers a knowledge-structure map and future research agenda.

items.title: Measuring Artificial Intelligence Integration in South African Private Higher Education: Applying a Refined Academic Quality Management Model
items.abstract: This study applies a refined model of Artificial Intelligence (AI) integration into Academic Quality Management Systems (AQMS) within South African private higher education. It builds on prior validation through exploratory factor analysis and reliability testing to examine how institutional factors relate to stakeholders’ perceptions of AI integration. Survey data from higher education and education technology stakeholders were analysed using PLS-SEM, correlation, multiple regression, and descriptive statistics. The results show moderate explanatory power, with regression indicating stronger overall model performance than PLS-SEM. Across analyses, Research Governance and Responsible AI Use emerged as the most consistent and statistically supported factor associated with AI_QMS. Strategic Planning and AI in Teaching and Learning also contributed positively, although their effects varied by method. In contrast, AI Literacy and Competency Development and Assessment and Evaluation produced inconsistent results, including negative regression coefficients, which are interpreted cautiously due to shared variance and measurement limitations. Other factors, including Ethical Considerations and Data Privacy, Environmental Impact, and Interdisciplinary Collaboration, did not demonstrate independent explanatory power in multivariable models. The findings highlight that observable institutional activity does not necessarily translate into consistent integration within academic quality systems. The study contributes a multi-dimensional framework that distinguishes between strongly supported relationships, method-dependent effects, and areas requiring further measurement development. Practically, the model provides institutions with a structured approach to assess and strengthen AI integration within academic quality management.

items.title: Model Degradation: Monitoring Human Activity Recognition with Classical Drift Detectors
items.abstract: This work investigates the impact of data drift on machine learning models deployed for Human Activity Recognition (HAR) using the UCI Human Activity Recognition Using Smartphones dataset. A Random Forest classifier is trained on an initial stable data distribution using a chronological split to reflect real-world deployment conditions. Model performance is first evaluated under no-drift conditions to establish a baseline. To study degradation, data drift is simulated by injecting Gaussian noise into the sensor features of future data, representing realistic changes such as sensor noise and calibration shifts. This controlled perturbation leads to a measurable decline in classification accuracy, precision, and recall, demonstrating the vulnerability of static models to evolving data distributions. Model degradation is monitored using the ADWIN (Adaptive Windowing) drift detection algorithm applied to the prediction error stream, enabling automatic identification of statistically significant performance changes. To mitigate degradation, a sliding-window retraining strategy is applied using recent samples, resulting in partial recovery of model performance. The results highlight the importance of time-aware evaluation, drift detection, and lightweight retraining for maintaining reliable machine learning systems in dynamic and resource-constrained environments.

items.title: Motivations and Constraints for Playing Electronic Games: A Scoping Review
items.abstract: The objective of this scoping review was to map the existing scientific literature on the relationship between motivations and constraints for playing digital games and esports, characterizing study profiles, identifying dominant themes and tensions, and examining the extent to which their interaction has been theorized and empirically investigated. Following Arksey and O'Malley’s framework and PRISMA-ScR guidelines, a search across EBSCO, SCOPUS, and Web of Science identified 38 eligible studies published between 1985 and 2025. The findings reveal a profound structural and theoretical imbalance: research is heavily skewed toward motivation-driven "pull factors" (76.3 %), while constraints remain critically understudied (13.2 %). Crucially, integrative studies (10.5 %) demonstrate that while intrinsic motivations can mitigate logistical barriers, deep psychosocial and symbolic constraints rooted in identity exclusion and social stigma consistently override motivation, triggering disengagement or severe affective costs. This review exposes the theoretical limitations of isolated psychological models, arguing for integrative, socio-culturally sensitive frameworks capable of capturing motivations and constraints as interdependent dynamics of the situated gaming experience.

items.title: Multi-dimensional hierarchical temporal alignment for improved temporal commonsense reasoning in large language models
items.abstract: Benefiting from recent advances in generative AI and large language models (LLMs), current LLM-driven AI systems are rapidly reshaping how we reason, plan, and make decisions. Yet endowing these systems with human-like temporal intelligence (e.g., understanding and comparing events across time) remains largely unresolved. To address this gap, we introduce a novel Multi-dimensional Hierarchical Temporal Alignment framework (denoted as MHTA), of which the core idea is to effectively ground the temporal alignment of an LLM in both event-specific and cross-event real-world temporal commonsense knowledge. Specifically, we first frame the temporal space as a multi-dimensional hierarchical space, where each dimension comprises its own set of temporal units. Building on this formulation, we curate an initial burn-in dataset in which annotations are constructed to reflect real-world human temporal commonsense in accordance with our defined temporal space. Based on the initial burn-in dataset, we propose two complementary fine-tuning objectives: (i) Grounding the temporal alignment in event-specific temporal commonsense knowledge, which is achieved through a novel hierarchy-preserving Wasserstein loss, and (ii) Grounding the temporal alignment in cross-event temporal commonsense knowledge, which is achieved via a margin-adaptive triplet loss. To evaluate the effectiveness of MHTA, we conduct extensive experiments on three representative benchmarks (MCTACO, DurationQA, and TimeDial). For example, on the MCTACO dataset, MHTA improves Mistral-7B by 6.0% in accuracy and 10.3% in exact match, and improves DeepSeek-LLM-7B by 5.4% in accuracy and 9.8% in exact match. Combined with different backbones, MHTA surpasses nearly all baselines across the three benchmarks and exceeds the performance of advanced models such as GPT-4o on MCTACO and DurationQA. These results demonstrate that MHTA provides consistent gains in temporal commonsense reasoning across diverse LLM backbones.

items.title: NEXT-GENERATION ADVANCEMENTS IN POLYMERIC MICRONEEDLES AND NANO CARRIER-MEDIATED TRANSDERMAL DRUG DELIVERY SYSTEMS
items.abstract: Transdermal drug delivery systems (TDDS) provide several advantages over conventional oral and parenteral routes, including avoidance of gastrointestinal degradation and hepatic first-pass metabolism, improved patient compliance, and controlled drug delivery. However, the stratum corneum acts as a major barrier, limiting the passive transport of hydrophilic and high-molecular-weight therapeutic agents. This review focuses on recent advances in polymeric microneedles and nanocarrier-mediated transdermal drug delivery systems developed to overcome these skin-permeation limitations. Literature from PubMed and Scopus was reviewed with emphasis on microneedle classification, polymeric biomaterials, nanocarrier systems, drug-loading capacity, permeation mechanisms, safety, and clinical translation. Polymeric microneedles, including solid, coated, dissolving, hydrogel-forming, and hollow systems, enable controlled and minimally painful delivery by creating temporary microchannels through the stratum corneum. Nanocarriers such as liposomes, ethosomes, solid lipid nanoparticles, nanostructured lipid carriers, polymeric nanoparticles, and inorganic nanoparticles further enhance dermal and transdermal drug transport through lipid fluidization, follicular pathways, and controlled drug deposition. The integration of these technologies provides promising opportunities for delivering macromolecules, vaccines, and localized therapeutics. Future developments involving stimuli-responsive systems, wearable biosensors, artificial intelligence, microfluidics, and personalized manufacturing may further enhance transdermal therapy. Despite challenges related to manufacturing scalability, regulatory standardization, and long-term biocompatibility, advanced microneedle and nanocarrier platforms have considerable potential for clinical translation and personalized drug delivery. Background: Traditional transdermal drug delivery systems (TDDS) provide a non-invasive, patient-compliant route that avoids gastrointestinal degradation and hepatic first-pass metabolism. However, the impermeable lipid matrix of the stratum corneum strictly limits the passive transport of molecules to those possessing specific hydrophobic profiles and low molecular weights. Objective: This comprehensive review examines contemporary physical and chemical breakthrough technologies, with specific focus on polymeric microneedles (MNs) and nanocarrier-facilitated delivery platforms engineered to overcome these macro-molecular transport constraints. Methodology: A systematic screening of literature from the PubMed and Scopus databases (spanning foundational models through 2026) was conducted to evaluate the mechanical structural properties, biopolymer selections, and systemic pharmacokinetics of advanced skin-permeation platforms. Results: Polymeric microneedles (dissolving, hydrogel-forming, and stimuli-responsive types) demonstrate precise disruption of the stratum corneum without contacting dermally located pain-sensitive nerve endings. Concurrently, lipidic, polymeric, and inorganic nanocarriers capitalize on hair follicles and transient lipid fluidization to deposit high-molecular-weight biologics, vaccines, and localized therapeutics. Conclusion: Combining active mechanical microneedles with target-specific nanocarriers represents the vanguard of modern personalized diagnostics and therapeutics, bridging laboratory innovation with clinical scale-up paradigms.

items.title: Novokult LLM: On the New Culture
items.abstract: Novokult LLM is a desktop application that runs a large language model on your own computer. It is built for left-wing organizers, researchers, and writers. Once a model file is on your machine, drafting, analysis, and chat can stay there. It has three modes: analysis of events and texts through a Marxist framework, agitprop drafting (leaflets, slogans, speeches, songs, strike bulletins), and free chat. You can load your own texts as a Sources Library, turn on web search routed through Tor, and export posters. The design starts from an argument. AI is machinery, and most of it is rented from a few firms that see every prompt. Novokult runs the machine where its users live and work, and its code is published under the Peer Production License, a copyfarleft license meant to keep it in common. The title of this paper names the older question behind that choice: who builds a movement's culture, and with what tools. The name Novokult contracts the Russian новая культура (novaya kultura), "new culture." Version 1.0.0 is built for Windows (portable and installer) and Linux (AppImage and deb). An Android port exists in the code but is unfinished.

items.title: On a conjecture of Sun on sums of four numbers x(5x±1)/2
items.abstract: Z.-W. Sun conjectured (arXiv:2411.14308, Conjecture 5.5) that every integer n > 51 can be written as w(5w−1)/2 + x(5x−1)/2 + y(5y+1)/2 + z(5z+1)/2 with w, x, y, z natural numbers. We prove the stronger statement that every natural number n except n = 1 and n = 19 has such a representation. The problem reduces to finding lattice points on a sphere in a coset of 10Z⁴ with exactly two negative coordinates. We detect these with a degree-8 polynomial weight, and bound the resulting theta series of weights 2 to 10 and level 400 through explicit newform decompositions and Deligne's bound. This leaves 8,167,125 explicit integers below 10¹⁰, which are checked directly. The proof is computer-assisted: the decompositions are certified in ball arithmetic and the polynomial inequality in exact arithmetic. An independent audit by a separate AI run recomputed every step with different code and found no error. All modular-forms constants were also re-derived independently in SageMath, without PARI/GP, and every constant matched. An external review by ChatGPT found no objection to the main proof; its wording points have been corrected. No human expert has yet checked the argument. The mathematics, code and audits were produced by the AI system Claude (Anthropic) under the author's direction; see Section 8 of the paper. This record contains the paper, all programs, certificates, logs and the audit report.

items.title: On the Issue of International Legal Guarantees for Personal Data Protection in the Context of Hybrid Warfare
items.abstract: This article investigates the complex problem of protecting human personal data during modern armed conflicts, particularly through the prism of hybrid warfare. The rapid pace of digitalization, the advancement of artificial intelligence technologies, and their active integration into the military sphere drive the relevance of this study. These factors cause fundamental changes in the methods and means of warfare, as well as in the very purpose of armed conflict. Today, informational influence and psychological pressure on the enemy's population - which are not always accompanied by a direct armed attack - constitute an integral component of any 21st-century military conflict. Consequently, the study analyzes the concept of hybrid warfare, defining it through characteristic features such as asymmetry, large-scale involvement of non-state actors, latency, and a combination of military and non-military means of struggle. The research specifically focuses on the role of generative artificial intelligence in the context of growing cyber threats. The paper emphasizes that unauthorized access to individuals' personal data during an armed conflict allows opposing parties to exert targeted psychological influence on population groups or individuals, manipulate public opinion through disinformation and «deepfakes,» and apply illegal filtration and terror against the population. Furthermore, this study analyzes the current international legal framework regarding personal data protection in conflict conditions. It examines the provisions of international humanitarian law, particularly the Fourth Geneva Convention of 1949. The findings establish that IHL norms lack special provisions for protecting digitized information. Moreover, ongoing discussions among researchers regarding the recognition of digital data as a «civilian object» significantly complicate the qualification of an enemy's actions in cyberspace as a violation of international humanitarian law. Finally, the article explores the provisions of specific international acts regulating data protection. The analysis determines that the permitted derogation from certain obligations in this sphere can lead to state abuses, often hidden behind the necessity of ensuring national security and defense. Ultimately, the paper highlights that international human rights law, through the provisions of international treaties and the case law of the ECtHR, establishes general guarantees to ensure compliance with the criteria of legality, strict necessity, and proportionality when interfering with the human right to personal data protection.

items.title: Opinion: Decisions without documents: Records continuity and evidential accountability in agentic supply chains
items.abstract: Agentic artificial intelligence is taking supply chain software from recommendation to execution. Planning and procurement agents now execute replenishment orders, reallocate freight, and negotiate with suppliers based on delegated powers, all without simultaneous human approval. Virtually every organization maintains the records of such activities as log files, subject only to IT retention policies until the files are no longer useful for diagnostic purposes and then disposed of. This opinion article contends that such treatment misclassifies what is, in substance, evidence of business transactions. An agent-executed decision that commits expenditure, alters a contractual position or redistributes risk across trading partners creates obligations that auditors, counterparties, regulators and courts may later test, and its trace therefore meets the functional definition of a record. Drawing on records continuum theory, the article follows a single agent decision across the dimensions of creation, capture, organisation and pluralisation and locates the points at which it leaves any recordkeeping regime. It then specifies the attributes of a trustworthy decision record in terms of reliability, authenticity and integrity, and proposes a governance arrangement in which records and information managers hold design authority over decision records alongside IT, procurement, legal and audit functions. The argument is addressed to information professionals in commercial settings who will increasingly be asked to evidence what an agent did, and on whose authority.
