items.title: PaReGTA: a temporally aware LLM-based patient representation framework for EHR analytics
items.abstract: Temporal information in structured electronic health records (EHRs) is often lost in sparse one-hot or count-based representations, while sequence models can be costly and data-hungry. We propose PaReGTA, an LLM-based encoding framework that (i) converts longitudinal EHR events into visit-level templated text with explicit temporal cues, (ii) learns domain-adapted visit embeddings via lightweight contrastive fine-tuning of a sentence-embedding model, and (iii) aggregates visit embeddings into a fixed-dimensional patient representation using hybrid temporal pooling that captures both recency and globally informative visits. The resulting fixed-dimensional patient representations can be used with conventional downstream machine-learning models. To examine factor-level sensitivity, we use PaReGTA-RSS (Representation Shift Score), a prespecified factor-removal analysis that recomputes patient representations after removing clinically defined factor groups and quantifies the resulting change in the fitted logit of a fixed logistic-regression model. We evaluated PaReGTA in a cohort of 39 088 patients with migraine from the All of Us Research Program (AoU) on a retrospective patient-level classification task with an EHR-derived target. In an exploratory comparison on the fixed held-out test cohort of 7818 patients, PaReGTA-Gap + LightGBM, used as a post hoc analytical reference, had the highest reported AUC, accuracy, and F1 values among the evaluated sparse, BERT-based EHR, and recurrent approaches in this cohort.

items.title: Pengaruh Literasi Digital terhadap Etika Penggunaan Artificial Intelligence pada Mahasiswa Perguruan Tinggi
items.abstract: The development of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in higher education has transformed the way students seek information, complete assignments, and understand academic materials. However, AI use also raises ethical issues, including plagiarism, overreliance on instant answers, and a lack of transparency in acknowledging AI assistance. This study aims to analyze the effect of digital literacy on the ethical use of AI among university students. A quantitative survey method was employed. Data were collected using a 1–5 Likert-scale questionnaire from 125 respondents, with 119 complete responses analyzed. Digital literacy was measured using 12 items, while ethical AI use was measured using 12 items. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, validity testing, reliability testing, correlation, and simple linear regression. The results show that digital literacy has a positive and significant effect on ethical AI use. The correlation coefficient of 0.638 indicates a strong relationship, while the coefficient of determination of 0.406 indicates that digital literacy explains 40.6% of the variation in ethical AI use. The regression equation is Y = 1.196 + 0.706X. These findings indicate that students with higher digital literacy tend to use AI more ethically, responsibly, and transparently. This study recommends strengthening digital literacy programs with an emphasis on AI ethics in higher education.

items.title: Physical activity, emotional intelligence and physical self-concept in Secondary Education teachers: a cross-sectional study
items.abstract: Teachers’ health and well-being are essential for promoting positive educational environments and healthy lifestyles within schools. Emotional intelligence and physical self-concept have emerged as relevant psychological factors associated with engagement in physical activity; however, evidence among secondary education teachers remains limited. The objective of this study was to analyse the relationships between physical activity, trait emotional intelligence and perceived physical self-concept among secondary education teachers, as well as to examine the indirect association between emotional intelligence and physical activity through physical self-concept. A cross-sectional study was conducted with 85 secondary education teachers from schools in the Region of Murcia (Spain). Participants completed the Trait Emotional Intelligence Questionnaire-Short Form (TEIQue-SF), the Physical Self-Concept Questionnaire (PSQ), and a physical activity assessment based on the PACE questionnaire. Descriptive analyses, Pearson correlations, MANOVA, and structural equation modelling were performed. Physical activity was positively associated with all dimensions of physical self-concept and with the sociability dimension of emotional intelligence. Teachers reporting higher levels of physical activity showed more favourable perceptions of their physical competence, condition, strength and self-esteem. In an exploratory structural equation model, emotional intelligence was positively associated with physical self-concept, which in turn was associated with physical activity; the indirect effect of emotional intelligence on physical activity through physical self-concept was significant (β = .18; 95% bootstrap CI [.03, .42]) and the direct effect was non-significant, a pattern statistically consistent with mediation that requires longitudinal confirmation. Physical activity is associated with better physical self-perceptions and greater emotional resources among secondary education teachers. These findings highlight the potential value of promoting active lifestyles within educational settings as a strategy to enhance teachers’ well-being and occupational health. Future longitudinal studies are needed to clarify the causal relationships among these variables.

Predictive machine maintenance usessensor data, Artificial Intelligence (AI), and Machine Learning (ML) to estimate when equipment may develop a fault. The system can thengenerate an alert so that maintenance is planned before failure occurs. This paper explains the concept, working process, major technologies, model design,applications, benefits, limitations, and a practical implementation framework. items.title: Predictive PLS-SEM Analysis of Artificial Intelligence Chatbots in Innovative Marketing
items.abstract: Marketing has witnessed a digital transformation driven by the fast evolution of technology and International Intelligence (AI), as businesses can now implement intelligent chatbot systems to boost customer interaction and improve the overall performance of the business. The study explores the relationships between Artificial Intelligence Chatbot Quality, Customer Trust, Perceived Ease of Use, Innovative Marketing Capability, Customer Experience, Supply Chain Integration and Business Performance, applying Predictive Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). A mediation analysis, PLSpredict, and Importance–Performance Map Analysis (IPMA) were used in SmartPLS 4 to analyse the primary data collected from 526 participants who have previously utilised AI-powered chatbots. The result show that AI Chatbot Quality significantly positively affects Innovative Marketing Capability and Customer Experience, and Customer Trust and Perceived Ease of Use positively influence Customer Experience. Customer Experience positively influences Supply Chain Integration and Business Performance and acts as a mediator between AI Chatbot Quality and Business Performance. The study combines the TAM and RBV models into a single predictive model, offering theoretical perspectives and practical implications for organisations looking to enable their AI chatbots to enhance their innovative marketing efforts and gain a sustainable competitive edge.
